The relay/credential question is trickier: the primary node is the most exposed (public-facing, previously compromised), so routing all archive traffic and credentials through it concentrates risk badly. I'm weighing whether a healthier, lower-exposure node with spare resources—like node-5 or node-2—should instead hold the uploader/relay role, separating credential custody from the compromised-history primary.

Pulling that apart, I realize dedicating a vault node would need new ingest endpoints on its agent, which is more build work than I want to scope right now. So for v1 I'll recommend keeping uploads on the primary as-is but hardening it: throttling, a streaming relay instead of a full mirror, and a second immutable copy sent via a write-only, delete-incapable key (Object Lock) to a separate provider — so even a compromised primary can't destroy backups, which limits blast radius without needing a new node role yet.

Thinking through where encryption should happen, I land on encrypting at the primary before upload using only the age public key, so plaintext never leaves RAM there and never touches the network unencrypted. The CPU cost is negligible at the bandwidth-limited upload speed, and I'm sketching a pipeline that pulls the file from the agent, hashes it, encrypts it, and streams it to storage via rclone with modest memory overhead — with simple whole-file retries on failure given the throttled transfer times are still reasonable for large files.

Working through total volume at the throttle rate, even a conservative daily/weekly load finishes comfortably within a few hours, so bandwidth isn't a real constraint on the network path. I also need to handle the primary's own local archives through the same upload pipeline, and reconsider whether the old node-mirror directory is even still needed — since with streaming relay, node archives already exist in two places (on-node and off-site), the mirror becomes redundant and can be retired once the new flow is verified.

Separately, node-5's near-full root disk needs a fix before enabling anything — moving the backup dataset to its own ZFS mount matching node-3's layout, something the owner handles manually. For the runner itself, I'm structuring it to loop through VMs one at a time rather than batching, so I can gate between guests and respect the time window, while tuning vzdump flags like bandwidth limit, I/O priority, worker count, and compression threads.

Checking throughput math: with bwlimit set around 78MiB/s against node-4's roughly 850GB of allocated disk, the backup window comes out to under two hours even accounting for vzdump reading zero blocks, comfortably inside the 4-5 hour window — and switching game VMs to weekly instead of daily backups would cut nightly load by roughly 4x.

If I rotate VMs through a weekly schedule by hashing vmid to day-of-week, each node only needs to back up about 1/7 of its fleet nightly, dropping node-4's load to roughly 120GB per night and shrinking local retention needs with keep-last-2 for two weekly fulls. But this changes the RPO for customer VMs from 1 day to 7 days, which is a real regression from the owner's stated "daily full backup, keep latest 3" policy — so I should flag this as a decision point rather than assume it, perhaps keeping daily backups for infra/platform VMs while rotating only the larger customer VMs weekly.

Actually, checking the math: even a throttled 80MiB/s daily backup of 850GB finishes in under 3 hours, well within the 4-hour window, so daily-for-all is still feasible without needing to downgrade cadence at all. I think the safest default is to keep daily throttled backups for every VM class initially, and expose a `cadenceDays`/rotate option in the policy schema so this can be tuned down later per class without baking in an RPO regression from day one.

Realizing daily off-site uploads of 345GB/day are way too heavy for Dropbox's bandwidth and quota, I'm splitting local vs off-site cadence: local backups stay daily for fast restores, while off-site shifts to weekly full images per VM, rotated across nights by a stable hash of VM ID so uploads spread evenly (~50GB/night) instead of flooding all at once. This gives local RPO of 24h and off-site RPO of about 7 days for VM images, with DB/platform/hypervisor configs still going off-site daily, and I'm now sizing retention—roughly 2 weekly + 1 monthly full cycle lands around 1TB, about a third of the 3TiB Dropbox quota.

I'm also weighing Dropbox against PBS: Dropbox works fine for a few hundred large files, but PBS's millions of small 4MB chunks would hammer Dropbox's API rate limits, so they're a mismatch. PBS itself looks appealing otherwise—dirty-bitmap incrementals cut nightly read/network load, built-in dedupe across cloned VMs saves storage, and it supports verification, pruning, sync jobs, and client-side encryption—though I need to account for VM restarts dropping the dirty bitmap and requiring a dedicated, secured box to run it on.

Weighing it all, PBS beats vzdump on load and RPO but demands new off-chassis infra that Dropbox can't satisfy since chunks don't sync there, so I'll recommend phase 1 as the improved vzdump+Dropbox setup with no new spend, and defer PBS as a phase 3 option once the fleet grows past roughly 2TB or daily RPO becomes a real requirement.

Now I'm sketching out the actual components to build: a gate script to decide whether backups run, a manifest writer, an age-based encryption wrapper for streaming and file encryption with sha256 verification, a per-node backup runner that's window-aware and gated behind an environment flag, and an offsite uploader that pulls from node agents and encrypts before uploading with rate limits.

For the uploader, I'm leaning toward writing it in TypeScript with pure, testable planner functions separate from the actual IO (which would shell out to rclone/age so it stays injectable and mockable). I want a dry-run plan mode that reads real inventories and manifests, though I'm weighing whether running that against live production data — since it touches the node token DB read-only — is appropriate within this session.

Since the collect script queries the production database directly and the rule against touching production data applies even to infrastructure-only tables, I'll avoid that path and instead feed the planner my SSH-gathered inventory JSON as fixtures, which still gives real validation without touching the DB. I'm also sketching a new read-only node-agent health endpoint that would return timer status, VM states, archive stats, disk usage, and load metrics.

Beyond that, I need to extend the backup path allowlist regex to cover the new hypervisor snapshot tarballs and manifest JSON files, since these are new output categories nodes will produce. Let me check whether there are existing node-agent tests I should look at before making these changes.

/**
 * Off-site (Mega) retention — pure decision logic for what to prune from the
 * Mega copy of the platform's backups.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS
 * ----------------
 * `scripts/backup-offsite.sh` mirrors `/tank/backup/{db,platform}` to a Mega
 * account via `megatools megacopy`. megacopy's own contract (see its manpage)
 * is explicit: "no files are ever overwritten or removed" — it is upload-only.
 * That is the right default for a tool that also does one-way *downloads*, but
 * it means Mega storage grows forever unless something else prunes it, even
 * though the LOCAL copies these files came from already rotate out on a
 * schedule (`scripts/backup-db.sh` deletes dumps past `NXEON_DB_RETENTION_DAYS`
 * (14d default); `scripts/backup-vms.sh` / `backup-pve-config.sh` keep only the
 * newest `NXEON_*_BACKUP_KEEP` archives (3 by default)).
 *
 * The two rclone/rsync targets `backup-offsite.sh` already supports don't have
 * this problem: `rclone sync` and `rsync --delete` both mirror the destination
 * to exactly match the source, so a file pruned locally is pruned remotely on
 * the very next run for free. Mega is the odd one out, so it needs an explicit
 * prune step — this module IS that step's decision logic, kept dependency-free
 * (no fs, no child_process, no clock — `now` is always passed in) so it can be
 * unit tested without a Mega account, a filesystem, or `megatools` installed.
 *
 * TWO RULES, applied together:
 *
 *  1. MIRROR: delete any remote file whose name is no longer present in the

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-node backup planner for the Nxeon backup runner (stdlib only).

Decides, for THIS node and TONIGHT, which guests are due for a local vzdump, in
what order, with which retention - from the guests Proxmox reports, the archives
already on disk and an optional owner policy file. Pure planning: it reads files
and prints JSON; it never runs vzdump or touches a guest.

Guest classes (see /root/research/backup-design.md section 4):
  infra         platform/infrastructure VMs (tag nxeon-infra, or an untagged
                running guest nobody can account for - treated as precious)
  customer-vps  a customer's general-purpose VPS
  game          a customer game server (named <family>-<id> by the provisioner)
  template      Proxmox templates (reproducible from scripts/build-templates.sh)

Policy file (/etc/nxeon/backup-policy.json, optional, hand-edited or exported by
scripts/backup-policy-export.ts):
  {"classDefaults": {"game": {"localCadenceDays": 1, "keepLast": 2}},
   "vms": {"105": {"class": "infra"}, "999": {"skip": true, "reason": "scratch"}}}

Output (stdout, JSON): {"vms": [...every guest with its class + decision...],
"due": [vmid, ... in run order], "node": ..., "today": ...}
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

GAME_FAMILIES = (
    "minecraft valheim rust palworld cs2 terraria ark satisfactory projectzomboid sdtd vrising enshrouded "
    "factorio gmod conan unturned theforest sonsoftheforest bedrock schedule1 dragonwilds sunkenland "
    "abioticfactor corekeeper icarus arkasa soulmask dst vintagestory necesse tf2 l4d2 nightingale squad "
    "spaceengineers kf2 barotrauma sandstorm mordhau theisle stationeers eco empyrion plutoniumt4 plutoniumt5 "
    "plutoniumt6 plutoniumiw5 armareforger arma3 cs16 ets2 ats dayz fivem"
).split()

# class -> defaults. localCadenceDays: how often THIS node makes a local archive.
# offsiteCadenceDays: how often a fresh copy must reach off-site storage (read by
# the primary's uploader, recorded here so the manifest is self-describing).
# priority: lower runs first (and is the last to be skipped when the window ends).
CLASS_DEFAULTS = {
    "infra":        {"priority": 0, "localCadenceDays": 1, "offsiteCadenceDays": 1,  "keepLast": 3},
    "customer-vps": {"priority": 1, "localCadenceDays": 1, "offsiteCadenceDays": 7,  "keepLast": 2},
    "game":         {"priority": 2, "localCadenceDays": 1, "offsiteCadenceDays": 7,  "keepLast": 2},
    "template":     {"priority": 9, "localCadenceDays": 7, "offsiteCadenceDays": 30, "keepLast": 1},
}

ARCHIVE_RE = re.compile(r"^vzdump-qemu-(\d+)-(\d{4})_(\d{2})_(\d{2})-(\d{2})_(\d{2})_(\d{2})\.vma(\.zst|\.gz|\.lzo)?$")


def classify(vm):
    """vm: dict(vmid, name, tags, template). Returns (class, why)."""
    tags = [t for t in re.split(r"[;, ]+", vm.get("tags") or "") if t]
    name = (vm.get("name") or "").lower()
    if vm.get("template"):
        return "template", "Proxmox template"
    if "nxeon-infra" in tags:
        return "infra", "tag nxeon-infra"
    fam = name.split("-", 1)[0]
    if fam in GAME_FAMILIES and len(name.split("-")) >= 2:
        return "game", "name prefix '%s' is a game family" % fam
    if any(t.startswith("user-") for t in tags):
        return "customer-vps", "customer-tagged guest"
    return "infra", "untagged guest - treated as platform infrastructure so it is never under-protected"


def newest_archives(archive_dir):
    """vmid -> newest archive datetime (UTC naive) by the timestamp in the file name."""
    out = {}
    try:
        names = os.listdir(archive_dir)
    except OSError:
        return out
    for n in names:
        m = ARCHIVE_RE.match(n)
        if not m:
            continue
        vmid = int(m.group(1))
        dt = datetime.datetime(*[int(m.group(i)) for i in range(2, 8)])
        if vmid not in out or dt > out[vmid]:
            out[vmid] = dt
    return out


def load_json(path, default):
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return default


def list_vms_live():
    raw = subprocess.run(["pvesh", "get", "/nodes/localhost/qemu", "--output-format", "json"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60, check=True).stdout
    return json.loads(raw)


def build_plan(vms, archives, state, policy, now):
    today = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    done_today = set(int(x) for x in (state or {}).get("done", []) if str(x).isdigit()) if (state or {}).get("day") == today else set()
    class_over = (policy or {}).get("classDefaults", {})
    vm_over = (policy or {}).get("vms", {})
    rows = []
    for vm in sorted(vms, key=lambda v: int(v["vmid"])):
        vmid = int(vm["vmid"])
        cls, why = classify(vm)
        over = vm_over.get(str(vmid), {})
        if over.get("class") in CLASS_DEFAULTS:
            cls, why = over["class"], "policy override"
        d = dict(CLASS_DEFAULTS[cls])
        d.update(class_over.get(cls, {}))
        d.update({k: v for k, v in over.items() if k in d})
        last = archives.get(vmid)
        age_days = None if last is None else (now - last).total_seconds() / 86400.0
        row = {
            "vmid": vmid, "name": vm.get("name"), "status": vm.get("status"), "class": cls, "why": why,
            "priority": d["priority"], "localCadenceDays": d["localCadenceDays"],
            "offsiteCadenceDays": d["offsiteCadenceDays"], "keepLast": d["keepLast"],
            "diskBytes": vm.get("maxdisk"), "lastArchive": None if last is None else last.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
            "ageDays": None if age_days is None else round(age_days, 2),
        }
        if over.get("skip"):
            row.update(decision="skip", reason=over.get("reason") or "policy skip")
        elif vmid in done_today:
            row.update(decision="done", reason="already backed up in tonight's window")
        elif last is None:
            row.update(decision="due", reason="never backed up locally")
        elif age_days is not None and age_days >= d["localCadenceDays"] - 0.25:
            # -0.25 d: a nightly run that started 5h later than yesterday must not skip tonight.
            row.update(decision="due", reason="newest archive is %.1f days old (cadence %s d)" % (age_days, d["localCadenceDays"]))
        else:
            row.update(decision="fresh", reason="newest archive is %.1f days old (cadence %s d)" % (age_days, d["localCadenceDays"]))
        rows.append(row)
    due = [r for r in rows if r["decision"] == "due"]
    # Never-backed-up first within a class (the riskiest gap), then oldest archive first.
    due.sort(key=lambda r: (r["priority"], 0 if r["lastArchive"] is None else 1, r["lastArchive"] or "", r["vmid"]))
    return {"today": today, "due": [r["vmid"] for r in due], "vms": rows}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--archives-dir", default="/tank/backup/platform")
    ap.add_argument("--state-file", default=None, help="run-state JSON {day, done: [vmid]} for tonight")
    ap.add_argument("--policy-file", default="/etc/nxeon/backup-policy.json")
    ap.add_argument("--vms-json", default=None, help="TEST ONLY: guest list JSON instead of pvesh")
    ap.add_argument("--now", default=None, help="TEST ONLY: ISO timestamp (UTC)")
    ap.add_argument("--node", default=os.uname().nodename)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    now = datetime.datetime.strptime(args.now, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S") if args.now else datetime.datetime.utcnow()
    vms = load_json(args.vms_json, []) if args.vms_json else list_vms_live()
    plan = build_plan(vms, newest_archives(args.archives_dir), load_json(args.state_file, {}) if args.state_file else {},
                      load_json(args.policy_file, {}), now)
    plan["node"] = args.node
    print(json.dumps(plan))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

and prints JSON; it never runs vzdump or touches a guest.

Guest classes (see /root/research/backup-design.md section 4):
  infra         platform/infrastructure VMs (tag nxeon-infra, or an untagged
                running guest nobody can account for - treated as precious)
  customer-vps  a customer's general-purpose VPS
  game          a customer game server (named <family>-<id> by the provisioner)
  template      Proxmox templates (reproducible from scripts/build-templates.sh)

Policy file (/etc/nxeon/backup-policy.json, optional, hand-edited or exported by
scripts/backup-policy-export.ts):
  {"classDefaults": {"game": {"localCadenceDays": 1, "keepLast": 2}},
   "vms": {"105": {"class": "infra"}, "999": {"skip": true, "reason": "scratch"}}}

Output (stdout, JSON): {"vms": [...every guest with its class + decision...],
"due": [vmid, ... in run order], "node": ..., "today": ...}
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

GAME_FAMILIES = (
    "minecraft valheim rust palworld cs2 terraria ark satisfactory projectzomboid sdtd vrising enshrouded "
    "factorio gmod conan unturned theforest sonsoftheforest bedrock schedule1 dragonwilds sunkenland "
    "abioticfactor corekeeper icarus arkasa soulmask dst vintagestory necesse tf2 l4d2 nightingale squad "
    "spaceengineers kf2 barotrauma sandstorm mordhau theisle stationeers eco empyrion plutoniumt4 plutoniumt5 "
    "plutoniumt6 plutoniumiw5 armareforger arma3 cs16 ets2 ats dayz fivem"
).split()

# class -> defaults. localCadenceDays: how often THIS node makes a local archive.
# offsiteCadenceDays: how often a fresh copy must reach off-site storage (read by
# the primary's uploader, recorded here so the manifest is self-describing).
# priority: lower runs first (and is the last to be skipped when the window ends).
CLASS_DEFAULTS = {
    "infra":        {"priority": 0, "localCadenceDays": 1, "offsiteCadenceDays": 1,  "keepLast": 3},
    "customer-vps": {"priority": 1, "localCadenceDays": 1, "offsiteCadenceDays": 7,  "keepLast": 2},
    "game":         {"priority": 2, "localCadenceDays": 1, "offsiteCadenceDays": 7,  "keepLast": 2},
    "template":     {"priority": 9, "localCadenceDays": 7, "offsiteCadenceDays": 30, "keepLast": 1},
}

ARCHIVE_RE = re.compile(r"^vzdump-qemu-(\d+)-(\d{4})_(\d{2})_(\d{2})-(\d{2})_(\d{2})_(\d{2})\.vma(\.zst|\.gz|\.lzo)?$")


def classify(vm):
    """vm: dict(vmid, name, tags, template). Returns (class, why)."""
    tags = [t for t in re.split(r"[;, ]+", vm.get("tags") or "") if t]
    name = (vm.get("name") or "").lower()
    if vm.get("template"):
        return "template", "Proxmox template"
    if "nxeon-infra" in tags:
        return "infra", "tag nxeon-infra"
    fam = name.split("-", 1)[0]
    if fam in GAME_FAMILIES and len(name.split("-")) >= 2:
        return "game", "name prefix '%s' is a game family" % fam
    if any(t.startswith("user-") for t in tags):
        return "customer-vps", "customer-tagged guest"
    return "infra", "untagged guest - treated as platform infrastructure so it is never under-protected"


def newest_archives(archive_dir):
    """vmid -> newest archive datetime (UTC naive) by the timestamp in the file name."""
    out = {}
    try:
        names = os.listdir(archive_dir)
    except OSError:
        return out
    for n in names:
        m = ARCHIVE_RE.match(n)
        if not m:
            continue
        vmid = int(m.group(1))
        dt = datetime.datetime(*[int(m.group(i)) for i in range(2, 8)])
        if vmid not in out or dt > out[vmid]:
            out[vmid] = dt
    return out


def load_json(path, default):
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return default


def list_vms_live():
    raw = subprocess.run(["pvesh", "get", "/nodes/localhost/qemu", "--output-format", "json"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60, check=True).stdout
    return json.loads(raw)


def build_plan(vms, archives, state, policy, now):
    today = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    done_today = set(int(x) for x in (state or {}).get("done", []) if str(x).isdigit()) if (state or {}).get("day") == today else set()
    class_over = (policy or {}).get("classDefaults", {})
    vm_over = (policy or {}).get("vms", {})
    rows = []
    for vm in sorted(vms, key=lambda v: int(v["vmid"])):
        vmid = int(vm["vmid"])
        cls, why = classify(vm)
        over = vm_over.get(str(vmid), {})
        if over.get("class") in CLASS_DEFAULTS:
            cls, why = over["class"], "policy override"
        d = dict(CLASS_DEFAULTS[cls])
        d.update(class_over.get(cls, {}))
        d.update({k: v for k, v in over.items() if k in d})
        last = archives.get(vmid)
        age_days = None if last is None else (now - last).total_seconds() / 86400.0
        row = {
            "vmid": vmid, "name": vm.get("name"), "status": vm.get("status"), "class": cls, "why": why,
            "priority": d["priority"], "localCadenceDays": d["localCadenceDays"],
            "offsiteCadenceDays": d["offsiteCadenceDays"], "keepLast": d["keepLast"],
            "diskBytes": vm.get("maxdisk"), "lastArchive": None if last is None else last.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
            "ageDays": None if age_days is None else round(age_days, 2),
        }
        if over.get("skip"):
            row.update(decision="skip", reason=over.get("reason") or "policy skip")
        elif vmid in done_today:
            row.update(decision="done", reason="already backed up in tonight's window")
        elif last is None:
            row.update(decision="due", reason="never backed up locally")
        elif age_days is not None and age_days >= d["localCadenceDays"] - 0.25:
            # -0.25 d: a nightly run that started 5h later than yesterday must not skip tonight.
            row.update(decision="due", reason="newest archive is %.1f days old (cadence %s d)" % (age_days, d["localCadenceDays"]))
        else:
            row.update(decision="fresh", reason="newest archive is %.1f days old (cadence %s d)" % (age_days, d["localCadenceDays"]))
        rows.append(row)
    due = [r for r in rows if r["decision"] == "due"]
    # Never-backed-up first within a class (the riskiest gap), then oldest archive first.
    due.sort(key=lambda r: (r["priority"], 0 if r["lastArchive"] is None else 1, r["lastArchive"] or "", r["vmid"]))
    return {"today": today, "due": [r["vmid"] for r in due], "vms": rows}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--archives-dir", default="/tank/backup/platform")
    ap.add_argument("--state-file", default=None, help="run-state JSON {day, done: [vmid]} for tonight")
    ap.add_argument("--policy-file", default="/etc/nxeon/backup-policy.json")
    ap.add_argument("--vms-json", default=None, help="TEST ONLY: guest list JSON instead of pvesh")
    ap.add_argument("--now", default=None, help="TEST ONLY: ISO timestamp (UTC)")
    ap.add_argument("--node", default=os.uname().nodename)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    now = datetime.datetime.strptime(args.now, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S") if args.now else datetime.datetime.utcnow()
    vms = load_json(args.vms_json, []) if args.vms_json else list_vms_live()
    plan = build_plan(vms, newest_archives(args.archives_dir), load_json(args.state_file, {}) if args.state_file else {},
                      load_json(args.policy_file, {}), now)
    plan["node"] = args.node
    print(json.dumps(plan))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
EOF

if [ "${V2}" != "1" ]; then
    log "inert: NXEON_BACKUP_V2 is not 1 in ${CONF} - the legacy nxeon-backup-vms timer is still the live backup (nothing done)"

    if [ "${NOW}" -ge "${s}" ] && [ "${NOW}" -lt $(( s + W_HOURS * 3600 )) ]; then WIN_START="${s}"; DAY="${d}"; break; fi
done
if [ -z "${WIN_START}" ]; then
    if [ "${FORCE}" = "1" ]; then
        WIN_START="${NOW}"; DAY="${TODAY}"; log "--force: ignoring the window; deadline is now + ${W_HOURS} h (the gate still applies)"
    else
        exit 0   # quiet: this fires every 15 min
    fi
fi

#   Network   interfaces, hosts, hostname, resolv, nftables + live `nft list ruleset`,
#             iptables-save (the NXEON_FWD DNAT chain is rebuilt from the DB, but the
#             dump documents what was live), /etc/nxeon (admin-ips.nft, agent-allow.nft)
#   Boot/disk fstab, mdadm.conf, partition tables (sfdisk -d), lsblk, modprobe.d
#             (ZFS ARC cap!), sysctl.d, /etc/zfs, zpool/zfs layout + local properties
#   Services  /etc/systemd/system (nxeon-* units, drop-ins, timers), node-agent files
#             and certs (/etc/nxeon/node-agent.*), /opt/nxeon-agent, cron
#   Access    sshd_config + host keys, /root/.ssh (authorized_keys, deploy keys)
#   Packages  dpkg selections, apt sources, pveversion -v
#   Snippets  cloud-init snippets (/tank/backup/snippets - the vendor snippet)
#

# ever stored locally at mode 0600 and is encrypted client-side (age) by the
# primary's uploader before it leaves the chassis - never uploaded in the clear.
#
#   nxeon-hypervisor-snapshot.sh          write the archive (default dest /tank/backup/hypervisor)
#   nxeon-hypervisor-snapshot.sh --list   print the include list and exit (reads nothing)
#

STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_HYPERVISOR_BACKUP_KEEP:-7}"

    /etc/pve /etc/vzdump.conf

    /etc/nftables.conf /etc/nxeon

    /etc/ssh/sshd_config /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key.pub

fail() {
    log "FAIL: $*"

[ -d /etc/pve ] || fail "/etc/pve is missing - not a Proxmox node?"

size=$(stat -c%s "${DEST}")
log "OK ${DEST} (${size} bytes, ${confs} VM definition(s), $(wc -l < "${list}") entries)"

mapfile -t old < <(ls -1t "${DEST_DIR}"/hypervisor-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | tail -n "+$((KEEP_LAST + 1))")
for f in "${old[@]:-}"; do [ -n "${f}" ] && { log "pruning ${f} (keep-last=${KEEP_LAST})"; rm -f -- "${f}"; }; done
printf '{"ok":true,"at":"%s","archive":"%s","bytes":%s,"vmDefinitions":%s}\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "${DEST}" "${size}" "${confs}" > "${STATUS_DIR}/hypervisor.json"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Platform snapshot (PRIMARY only): everything that is not a VM and not the
# database but that you cannot rebuild the platform without.
#
#   Secrets   /opt/nxeon/.env, /opt/nxeon/.kodely-secrets.local, /opt/nxeon-secrets,
#             /root/nxeon-credentials.txt, /root/nxeon-dns-records.txt,
#             mail credentials + DKIM (/etc/nxeon), the rclone config (Dropbox token)
#   Web       /etc/nginx (vhosts), /etc/letsencrypt (certs + ACME account keys),
#             /etc/postfix, /etc/postgresql (server config), /etc/fail2ban
#   Code      `git bundle --all` of /opt/nxeon (every branch, INCLUDING commits not
#             yet pushed to origin) + uncommitted/untracked working-tree changes
#   Data      /opt/nxeon/data, board-uploads (admin kanban attachments), partner-files
#   Database  `pg_dumpall --globals-only` (roles + passwords - the per-database
#             dumps from backup-db.sh do not contain them)
#   DNS       Cloudflare zone export (BIND format) for every zone the token can read,
#             when CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is available - skipped, loudly, if not
#   Misc      crontab, `crontab -l` of root, apt manual packages
#
# Everything here is sensitive. The archive is written at mode 0600 and is
# encrypted client-side (age) before it leaves this chassis.
#
#   nxeon-platform-snapshot.sh          write the archive (default /tank/backup/platform-extra)
#   nxeon-platform-snapshot.sh --list   print what would be included and exit (reads nothing)
#
# Exit 0 ok, 1 failed. A missing OPTIONAL path is a note, a missing REQUIRED path
# (the .env, the git repo) is a failure - a platform snapshot without them is not a
# snapshot, and a green status would be a lie.
set -uo pipefail

APP="${NXEON_APP_DIR:-/opt/nxeon}"
DEST_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_EXTRA_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform-extra}"
STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_PLATFORM_EXTRA_KEEP:-4}"
TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
DEST="${DEST_DIR}/platform-${TS}.tar.gz"

REQUIRED=( "${APP}/.env" "${APP}/.git" )
OPTIONAL=(
    "${APP}/.kodely-secrets.local" /opt/nxeon-secrets /root/nxeon-credentials.txt /root/nxeon-dns-records.txt
    /root/.config/rclone
    /etc/nginx /etc/letsencrypt /etc/postfix /etc/postgresql /etc/fail2ban
    "${APP}/data" "${APP}/board-uploads" "${APP}/partner-files"
)

if [ "${1:-}" = "--list" ]; then
    printf 'REQUIRED %s\n' "${REQUIRED[@]}"; printf 'OPTIONAL %s\n' "${OPTIONAL[@]}"
    echo "GENERATED git-bundle-all, git-dirty.patch, untracked.tar, pg-globals.sql, cloudflare-dns/*.zone, crontab-root.txt"
    exit 0
fi

log() { echo "[$(date -u +%FT%TZ)] $*"; }
fail() {
    log "FAIL: $*"; mkdir -p "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null
    printf '{"ok":false,"at":"%s","error":"%s"}\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" > "${STATUS_DIR}/platform-extra.json" 2>/dev/null
    exit 1
}

mkdir -p "${DEST_DIR}" "${STATUS_DIR}" || fail "cannot create ${DEST_DIR}"
chmod 700 "${DEST_DIR}"; chmod 755 "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null
for r in "${REQUIRED[@]}"; do [ -e "$r" ] || fail "required path ${r} is missing"; done

work="$(mktemp -d /tmp/nxeon-platform.XXXXXX)" || fail "mktemp"
trap 'rm -rf "${work}"' EXIT
gen="${work}/generated"; mkdir -p "${gen}"; chmod 700 "${work}"

git -C "${APP}" bundle create "${gen}/nxeon-all.bundle" --all >/dev/null 2>"${work}/git.err" || fail "git bundle failed: $(head -c 200 "${work}/git.err")"
git -C "${APP}" bundle verify "${gen}/nxeon-all.bundle" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "git bundle did not verify"
git -C "${APP}" rev-parse HEAD > "${gen}/git-HEAD.txt"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Client-side encryption helper for Nxeon backups (age, X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305).
#
# WHY age AND WHY A PUBLIC KEY: backups hold customer data and every platform
# secret. They are encrypted BEFORE they leave the chassis, to a PUBLIC key that
# lives on the box (/etc/nxeon/backup-recipients.txt). The matching PRIVATE key
# (identity) is held by the owner OFF this machine. A thief or a compromised
# primary can therefore upload new backups but can NOT read any old one, and the
# key cannot be lost with the box it is meant to rescue. This script refuses to
# run if it ever finds an age SECRET key in the recipients file.
#
#   nxeon-backup-crypt.sh check                          validate the recipients file
#   nxeon-backup-crypt.sh encrypt <src|-> <dest.age>     encrypt; prints one JSON meta line
#   nxeon-backup-crypt.sh decrypt <src.age> <identity-file> [dest|-]
#   nxeon-backup-crypt.sh keygen <identity-out> <recipients-out>   (RUN ON THE OWNER'S OWN MACHINE)
#
# Env: NXEON_BACKUP_RECIPIENTS (default /etc/nxeon/backup-recipients.txt), AGE_BIN (default age).
# `encrypt` hashes plaintext and ciphertext in the same single read pass (no second
# read of a 20 GB archive). Meta JSON: {"plainBytes","plainSha256","bytes","sha256"}.
set -uo pipefail
RECIP="${NXEON_BACKUP_RECIPIENTS:-/etc/nxeon/backup-recipients.txt}"
AGE="${AGE_BIN:-age}"
KEYGEN="${AGE_KEYGEN_BIN:-age-keygen}"

die() { echo "nxeon-backup-crypt: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
need_age() { command -v "${AGE}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "age not found (apt install age, or set AGE_BIN)"; }

check_recipients() {
    [ -f "${RECIP}" ] || die "recipients file ${RECIP} missing - refusing to produce an UNENCRYPTED backup"
    grep -q 'AGE-SECRET-KEY' "${RECIP}" && die "${RECIP} contains an age SECRET key. The private key must never live on the machine being backed up - remove it and keep it off-box"
    local n; n="$(grep -cE '^age1[a-z0-9]+$' "${RECIP}")"
    [ "${n}" -ge 1 ] || die "${RECIP} holds no age1... public key"
    [ "${n}" -ge 2 ] || echo "nxeon-backup-crypt: WARNING only ONE recipient configured - add an escrow key so a single lost key cannot lock you out" >&2
    echo "${n}"
}

cmd="${1:-}"; shift || true
case "${cmd}" in
    check)
        need_age; n="$(check_recipients)" || exit 1; echo "ok: ${n} recipient(s)"
        ;;
    encrypt)
        src="${1:-}"; dest="${2:-}"; [ -n "${src}" ] && [ -n "${dest}" ] || die "usage: encrypt <src|-> <dest.age>"
        need_age; check_recipients >/dev/null || exit 1
        [ "${src}" = "-" ] || [ -f "${src}" ] || die "source ${src} not found"
        tmp="${dest}.partial"; mkdir -p "$(dirname "${dest}")"
        ps="$(mktemp)"; cs="$(mktemp)"; pb="$(mktemp)"; cb="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "${ps}" "${cs}" "${pb}" "${cb}" "${tmp}"' EXIT
        { if [ "${src}" = "-" ]; then cat; else cat -- "${src}"; fi; } \
          | tee >(sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1 > "${ps}") >(wc -c > "${pb}") \
          | "${AGE}" -R "${RECIP}" \
          | tee >(sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1 > "${cs}") >(wc -c > "${cb}") > "${tmp}"
        rcs=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")
        for c in "${rcs[@]}"; do [ "${c}" -eq 0 ] || die "pipeline failed (${rcs[*]})"; done
        sync_wait=0; while [ ! -s "${cs}" ] || [ ! -s "${cb}" ]; do sleep 0.2; sync_wait=$((sync_wait+1)); [ "${sync_wait}" -gt 100 ] && die "hash helpers did not finish"; done
        sleep 0.2
        mv "${tmp}" "${dest}"; chmod 600 "${dest}"
        printf '{"plainBytes":%s,"plainSha256":"%s","bytes":%s,"sha256":"%s"}\n' "$(tr -d ' \n' < "${pb}")" "$(cat "${ps}")" "$(tr -d ' \n' < "${cb}")" "$(cat "${cs}")"
        trap - EXIT; rm -f "${ps}" "${cs}" "${pb}" "${cb}"
        ;;
    decrypt)
        src="${1:-}"; ident="${2:-}"; dest="${3:--}"; [ -f "${src}" ] && [ -f "${ident}" ] || die "usage: decrypt <src.age> <identity-file> [dest|-]"
        need_age
        if [ "${dest}" = "-" ]; then "${AGE}" -d -i "${ident}" -- "${src}"; else "${AGE}" -d -i "${ident}" -o "${dest}" -- "${src}"; fi
        ;;
    keygen)
        idf="${1:-}"; rf="${2:-}"; [ -n "${idf}" ] && [ -n "${rf}" ] || die "usage: keygen <identity-out> <recipients-out>"
        command -v "${KEYGEN}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "age-keygen not found"
        [ -e "${idf}" ] && die "${idf} already exists - refusing to overwrite a key"
        ( umask 077; "${KEYGEN}" -o "${idf}" 2>/dev/null )
        "${KEYGEN}" -y "${idf}" >> "${rf}"
        echo "identity (PRIVATE, keep OFF the servers): ${idf}"; echo "recipient (PUBLIC, goes to /etc/nxeon/backup-recipients.txt): $(tail -1 "${rf}")"
        ;;
    *) die "usage: $0 {check|encrypt|decrypt|keygen} ..." ;;
esac
EOF

    check)
        need_age; n="$(check_recipients)" || exit 1; echo "ok: ${n} recipient(s)"
        ;;
    encrypt)
        src="${1:-}"; dest="${2:-}"; [ -n "${src}" ] && [ -n "${dest}" ] || die "usage: encrypt <src|-> <dest.age>"
        need_age; check_recipients >/dev/null || exit 1
        [ "${src}" = "-" ] || [ -f "${src}" ] || die "source ${src} not found"
        tmp="${dest}.partial"; mkdir -p "$(dirname "${dest}")"
        ps="$(mktemp)"; cs="$(mktemp)"; pb="$(mktemp)"; cb="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "${ps}" "${cs}" "${pb}" "${cb}" "${tmp}"' EXIT
        { if [ "${src}" = "-" ]; then cat; else cat -- "${src}"; fi; } \
          | tee >(sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1 > "${ps}") >(wc -c > "${pb}") \
          | "${AGE}" -R "${RECIP}" \
          | tee >(sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1 > "${cs}") >(wc -c > "${cb}") > "${tmp}"
        rcs=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")
        for c in "${rcs[@]}"; do [ "${c}" -eq 0 ] || die "pipeline failed (${rcs[*]})"; done
        sync_wait=0; while [ ! -s "${cs}" ] || [ ! -s "${cb}" ]; do sleep 0.2; sync_wait=$((sync_wait+1)); [ "${sync_wait}" -gt 100 ] && die "hash helpers did not finish"; done
        sleep 0.2
        mv "${tmp}" "${dest}"; chmod 600 "${dest}"
        printf '{"plainBytes":%s,"plainSha256":"%s","bytes":%s,"sha256":"%s"}\n' "$(tr -d ' \n' < "${pb}")" "$(cat "${ps}")" "$(tr -d ' \n' < "${cb}")" "$(cat "${cs}")"
        trap - EXIT; rm -f "${ps}" "${cs}" "${pb}" "${cb}"
        ;;
    decrypt)
        src="${1:-}"; ident="${2:-}"; dest="${3:--}"; [ -f "${src}" ] && [ -f "${ident}" ] || die "usage: decrypt <src.age> <identity-file> [dest|-]"
        need_age
        if [ "${dest}" = "-" ]; then "${AGE}" -d -i "${ident}" -- "${src}"; else "${AGE}" -d -i "${ident}" -o "${dest}" -- "${src}"; fi
        ;;
    keygen)
        idf="${1:-}"; rf="${2:-}"; [ -n "${idf}" ] && [ -n "${rf}" ] || die "usage: keygen <identity-out> <recipients-out>"
        command -v "${KEYGEN}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "age-keygen not found"
        [ -e "${idf}" ] && die "${idf} already exists - refusing to overwrite a key"
        ( umask 077; "${KEYGEN}" -o "${idf}" 2>/dev/null )
        "${KEYGEN}" -y "${idf}" >> "${rf}"
        echo "identity (PRIVATE, keep OFF the servers): ${idf}"; echo "recipient (PUBLIC, goes to /etc/nxeon/backup-recipients.txt): $(tail -1 "${rf}")"
        ;;
    *) die "usage: $0 {check|encrypt|decrypt|keygen} ..." ;;
esac

STATUS REPORT (paused at the owner's request, ~03:50 UTC 2026-10-03). The audit is done and the design decisions are made. About half of the build is done and tested. Nothing was applied to any node or VM.

BRANCH / COMMIT
- Branch `feature/complete-offsite-backups`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-backups` (node_modules is a real `cp -a` copy).
- WIP commit `42d4e88cdd`. Explicit paths only. I committed with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` so the post-commit auto-push hook could not fire. Nothing was pushed.
- Notes: `/root/agent-notes/backups.md`. Design and audit: `/root/research/backup-design.md`. It has the full coverage matrix, the decisions, the projection and a "RESUME HERE" list.
- Nothing is running in the background and no SSH sessions are open. I wrote no files on any node; I ran Python scripts on nodes by piping them over stdin, read-only.
- Scratch left on the primary: `/tank/age-test` (a real `age` binary extracted with `apt-get download` + `dpkg-deb -x`, not installed). Remove it, or keep it for the tests (set `AGE_BIN` and `AGE_KEYGEN_BIN`).

- **Off-site:** the timer exists only in `/etc/systemd/system` (not in `deploy/`) and is disabled. The last real upload was 2026-09-14 (database and host-config only). VM archives on Dropbox are from 2026-09-12 (214 files, 367.8 GiB). `offsite.json` still says ok:true, which is a stale green. Someone made `manual-catchup-2026-10-03/` today (274 MiB); I did not touch it.
- **Plaintext secrets on Dropbox:** nothing is encrypted. The host-config tar already on Dropbox holds the PVE private keys, Cloudflare tokens, mail credentials, DKIM and `.env` in clear.
- **node-5 (BHS):**
  - The backup timer is disabled and inactive.
  - `/tank/backup` is a plain directory on the 20 GB root filesystem, 96% full with 811 MB free.
  - 5 of its 8 VMs (147, 148, 645, 650, 651) have no backup anywhere. The other 3 are 4 days stale.
  - It was never collected by the primary's mirror.
- **node-4:** swap is 2/2 GB full and only 1.9 GB RAM is available. VMs 648 and 649 have no backup yet. Node-4's VMs were last pulled on 09-16 and have never reached off-site.
- **Primary and node-4:** both are memory-starved, so any added load needs gating.
- **node-2 and node-3:** local backups are fresh and healthy. Their off-site copies are stale.
- **Not backed up anywhere:**
  - Postgres roles and passwords (no `pg_dumpall --globals`).
  - WAL and PITR (`archive_mode` is off).
  - `/etc/letsencrypt`, the nft ruleset, `modprobe.d` (ARC caps), the ZFS layout and cloud-init snippets.
  - The rclone/Dropbox config. It is the only copy of the key to the vault.
  - `/opt/nxeon-secrets`, `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`, `board-uploads` (701 MB) and `data/`.
  - Unpushed git branches, and uncommitted work in `/opt/nxeon`.
  - A Cloudflare DNS export.
  - Customer on-demand backups (114-167 GB per node) are local only.
- **Orphans:** about 60 GB of local archives for VMs that no longer exist, and the same VMIDs still on Dropbox.
- **VMID 114** exists on two nodes (primary darkeden-guard-sg, node-2 skyora-prod). The off-site layout includes the node name so archives cannot collide.
- **Load measurements:**
  - `vzdump` runs unthrottled at 260-1000 MiB/s read.
  - `ionice`, `IOSchedulingClass` and `IOWeight` do nothing on these NVMe drives (scheduler is `none`). The real throttle is `vzdump --bwlimit`.
  - The guest fs-freeze lasts 1 s or less (56 historic logs), so game-server stall risk is negligible.
  - Primary run: 37 min, 26 CPU-min.
  - The vms timer at 04:30 UTC is 12:30 in Singapore.
- **Dropbox:** the env file says the plan is a Plus one-month free trial from 2026-09-12, so it ends around 2026-10-12.

DESIGN DECISIONS MADE
- **Two tiers.** Local, per node, RPO 24 h. Off-site is Dropbox, with cadence by class:
  - infra: daily
  - customer VPS: weekly
  - game: weekly
  - template: monthly, from one node only
  This keeps the nightly upload at about 50-60 GB instead of 345 GB.
- **Layout:** `nxeon-backups/<YYYY>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<node>/{hypervisor,vms/<vmid>-<name>,databases,platform}`, with `manifest.json` and a README per run. File contents are `.age`; names and the manifest are plain.
- **Encryption:** `age`, with only the public key on the box and the private identity held off-box by the owner. The helper refuses a recipients file that contains a secret key, and warns on a single recipient so you add an escrow key. Verified with the real `age` binary:
  - round trip works
  - plaintext is absent from the stored object
  - a different identity cannot decrypt
- **Upload path:** the primary alone holds the Dropbox credential. It streams from each node-agent through `age` into `rclone rcat`, with no staging on disk and no mirror. Retire the `/tank/backup/nodes` mirror after verification. The primary was root-compromised on 2026-09-06 and can delete Dropbox, so I recommend a second write-only or Object-Lock copy of the small critical set (database, platform, hypervisor, about 10 GB) at another provider.
- **Performance safety (built):**
  - Sequential per-VM `vzdump` in snapshot mode with `--bwlimit` (60 MiB/s, 20 on starved nodes), `--zstd 1` and `max-workers=1`.
  - One job per node, via `flock`.
  - A hard stop at the end of the window; the next tick or night resumes.
  - A gate before every unit that checks:
    - PSI for cpu, io and memory
    - swap activity rate (not swap level)
    - a MemAvailable floor
    - load per CPU
    - other heavy jobs
    - ZFS ARC no-grow, which switches to a "gentle" profile
  - "pause" waits up to 30 min, then stops for the night. "abort" stops at once.
  - I ran the gate read-only on nodes 3, 4 and 5 just now. All returned go; nodes 3 and 4 were gentle. Node-4 would be slowed, not blocked.
- **Backup windows:** chosen per node from player-session telemetry, with visits as a weak tie-break. Fallback is region-local 02:00 when there is less than 7 days or 20 player-hours of data. Fallback values today:
  - SGP nodes: 18:00 UTC
  - FSN: 00:00 UTC
  - BHS: 06:00 UTC
  I did not read the production DB, so the real windows are not computed yet.
- **Freshness checks:**
  - A disabled timer is CRITICAL immediately (the 09-15 failure is a test).
  - An unreadable remote is CRITICAL, not OK.
  - Also covered: stale per category, node or VM; node timer off; VMs never backed up; disk too small for the next archive; unencrypted uploads; quota; restore-test age.
  - It is designed to feed the existing `lib/fleet-alert-plan.ts` with the prefix `OFFSITE-BACKUP:`. Not wired yet.
- **Retention** (dry-run by default; it never deletes for a node it could not read):
  - database, hypervisor and platform: 7 daily, 4 weekly, 6 monthly
  - infra VM: 3 daily, 2 weekly, 1 monthly
  - customer VPS: 2 weekly, 1 monthly
  - game: 1 weekly, 1 monthly
  - template: 2 monthly
  - deleted-VM backups are purged 30 days after the newest copy
  - hard cap of 400 deletions per run
- **Catch-up for the 19-day gap:** a byte budget of 160 GiB per run and at most 60 files. Database, platform and hypervisor go first, then infra VMs. It re-plans from the remote listing each run, so it is idempotent.
- **Projected Dropbox usage:** about 0.9 TB, around 30% of 3 TiB, at steady state. This is an upper bound built on stated assumptions; the first retention pass purges today's stale 368 GiB.

WHAT IS BUILT (inert, all tests pass under tsx)
- `scripts/backup/`: `nxeon-backup-gate.py`, `nxeon-backup-plan.py`, `nxeon-backup-node.sh` (flag `NXEON_BACKUP_V2`, inert by default), `nxeon-hypervisor-snapshot.sh`, `nxeon-platform-snapshot.sh`, `nxeon-backup-crypt.sh`.
- `lib/`: `backup-layout.ts`, `backup-offsite-plan.ts`, `backup-window.ts`, `backup-freshness.ts`, `backup-stream.ts`.
- `node-agent/index.js`: read-only `GET /v1/backup/health`, plus an allowlist for `hypervisor/` and the new status files.
- Tests: `test/backup-{gate,plan,layout,offsite-plan,window,freshness,stream,crypt,node-runner}.test.ts`.
- The tests found four real bugs, all fixed:
  - `vzdump` runs as `perl /usr/bin/vzdump`, so the gate missed it.
  - `date -d "@N -1 day"` is invalid, which would have broken windows that cross midnight.
  - `rclone rcat` uploads an empty object when `age` dies. It is now deleted, and the planner ignores objects under 150 bytes.
  - The EPIPE error hid the real cause.

NOT DONE (precise resume list is in the design doc)
1. Test for the agent health endpoint. It is only syntax-checked.
2. Agent client call `agentBackupHealth`, and the local collector for the primary.
3. Uploader CLI `scripts/backup-offsite-run.ts`: `--plan` by default; `--execute` needs `NXEON_OFFSITE_V2=1`. It writes the manifest and an honest `offsite.json`.
4. Worker sweep `worker/offsite-backup-sweep.ts`, flag `NXEON_OFFSITE_FRESHNESS`; add the `OFFSITE-BACKUP:` prefix.
5. Admin panel in `/admin/backups` with the coverage matrix and findings.
6. `scripts/backup-window-report.ts` and `scripts/backup-policy-export.ts` (read-only DB; for the owner to run, not for agents against prod).
7. `deploy/backup/`: run, offsite and freshness units and timers (this adds the missing offsite timer file), a slice with CPU, memory and IO limits, a `vzdump.conf` template and example env files.
8. Weekly restore-test script, using a never-reused scratch VMID, with a dry-run test.
9. Rewrite `docs/DISASTER-RECOVERY.md` (rebuild from nothing, node rebuild, key recovery), add the `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` section and change-history bullet, and tick `ROADMAP.md`.
10. `npx tsc --noEmit` has NOT been run on the new TS.
11. Still to write in the design doc: the Proxmox Backup Server evaluation (draft verdict: technically better, but it needs a separate always-on host and cannot target Dropbox), the ZFS send/recv incremental option, data-only game backups (phase 2, not built), the staged rollout, and rollback.

OWNER DECISIONS ALREADY KNOWN
- Where the age private key lives. I suggest a password manager, a printed paper copy, and a second escrow recipient held elsewhere. It must never be on any server.
- A second write-only or immutable copy of the small critical set at another provider.
- Whether Dropbox stays the vault, and the plan after the trial ends (around 2026-10-12).
- **Node-5 first step, before enabling anything there:** create a ZFS dataset `data/backup` mounted at `/tank/backup`. The root filesystem has 811 MB free.
- Off-site RPO for customer VPS and game VMs is 7 days in this design, versus the earlier "daily". Daily game data needs the phase-2 data-only engine.
- Whether customer on-demand backups should go off-site.
- Retire the `/tank/backup/nodes` mirror once streaming upload is proven.
- The purge window for deleted customers' backups (default 30 days).
- Approval to delete about 60 GB of orphan local archives.
- Review the `manual-catchup-2026-10-03` folder someone made on Dropbox.

COULD NOT VERIFY
- Real quiet windows from production telemetry.
- Dropbox plan and quota after the trial.
- A real Dropbox upload (nothing was uploaded).
- Restore from an encrypted archive on a real node.
- The agent health endpoint, and `tsc`.

content.text:
The audit and design are done and about half the build is finished, but I paused at your request. Nothing has been applied to any node or VM. The remaining work and the owner rollout steps are in the notes below.

- **Branch and commit:** `feature/complete-offsite-backups`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-backups`, WIP commit `42d4e88cdd`. I committed with hooks disabled so the auto-push could not fire; nothing was pushed.
- **Tests:** the new tests pass under `tsx`. The new TypeScript has not been run through `tsc --noEmit`, and the new node-agent health endpoint is only syntax-checked, with no test yet.
- **Notes:** `/root/research/backup-design.md` has the full coverage matrix, the decisions and a "RESUME HERE" list. `/root/agent-notes/backups.md` has the status.
- **Scratch:** `/tank/age-test` on the primary holds a real `age` binary, extracted from the Debian package, not installed. The stream and crypt tests use it through `AGE_BIN` and `AGE_KEYGEN_BIN`, so keep it or delete it.
- **Running state:** no background jobs or SSH sessions are left open, and I left no files on any node.

## Coverage matrix: key findings (all 5 nodes, read-only)

- **Off-site is stalled.** The timer exists only in `/etc/systemd/system` (not in `deploy/`) and is disabled. The last real upload was 2026-09-14, and VM archives on Dropbox are from 2026-09-12. `offsite.json` still says ok:true.
- **Secrets are on Dropbox in clear.** Nothing is encrypted, and the host-config tar already there holds the PVE private keys, Cloudflare tokens, mail credentials and `.env`.
- **Node-5 is unprotected.** Its timer is disabled and `/tank/backup` sits on the 20 GB root filesystem, 96% full with 811 MB free. VMs 147, 148, 645, 650 and 651 have no backup anywhere, and it was never collected by the primary.
- **Node-4 is behind and starved.** VMs 648 and 649 have no backup yet, and nothing from node-4 has reached off-site. It has swap full and 1.9 GB RAM available.
- **Nodes 2 and 3** have fresh local backups but stale off-site copies.
- **Not backed up anywhere:**
  - Postgres roles and passwords, and WAL/PITR (`archive_mode` is off).
  - `/etc/letsencrypt`, the nft ruleset, `modprobe.d` ARC caps, ZFS layout, cloud-init snippets and the `rclone.conf` with the Dropbox token.
  - `/opt/nxeon-secrets`, the credentials file, `board-uploads` and `data/`.
  - Unpushed git branches and uncommitted work in `/opt/nxeon`, and a Cloudflare DNS export.
  - Customer on-demand backups (114-167 GB per node) are local only.
- **Smaller findings:**
  - About 60 GB of local archives belong to VMs that no longer exist.
  - VMID 114 exists on two nodes (primary and node-2).
  - Someone created `manual-catchup-2026-10-03/` on Dropbox; I did not touch it.
  - The env file says Dropbox is a Plus one-month free trial from 2026-09-12, so it ends around 2026-10-12.
- **Load profile:** vzdump runs unthrottled at 260-1000 MB/s read, and the 04:30 UTC timer is lunchtime in Singapore. `ionice` and `IOWeight` do nothing on these NVMe drives (scheduler `none`), so `vzdump --bwlimit` is the only real read throttle.
- **Freeze stalls are not a risk:** the guest fs-freeze lasts 1 s or less across 56 historic logs.

## Design decisions made

- **Two tiers.** Local backups per node (RPO 24 h) plus off-site on Dropbox. Off-site cadence follows guest class: infra daily, customer VPS and game weekly, templates monthly from one node only. That keeps the nightly upload to about 50-60 GB instead of 345 GB.
- **Layout.** `nxeon-backups/<YYYY>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<node>/{hypervisor,vms/<vmid>-<name>,databases,platform}`, with a plain manifest and README per run and `.age` contents.
- **Encryption** is `age`, with only the public key on the box and the private key held off-box by the owner. The helper refuses a recipients file containing a secret key and warns on a single recipient. I verified it against the real `age` binary: round trip works, plaintext is absent from the stored object, and a different key cannot decrypt.
- **Upload path.** The primary alone holds the Dropbox credential. It streams from each node-agent through `age` into `rclone rcat`, with no staging on disk and no mirror. The primary was root-compromised on 2026-09-06 and can delete Dropbox, so I recommend a second write-only copy of the small critical set (database, platform, hypervisor, about 10 GB) elsewhere.
- **Performance safety (built).**
  - One job per node, sequential `vzdump` in snapshot mode with `--bwlimit` (60 MiB/s, or 20 on starved nodes).
  - A hard stop at the window's end, with resume next night.
  - A gate before each unit that watches PSI, swap activity, free RAM, load, other heavy jobs and ZFS ARC state, and slows down to a "gentle" profile on starved nodes.
  - I ran the gate read-only on nodes 3, 4 and 5 just now: all returned go, with nodes 3 and 4 gentle. Node-4 would be slowed, not blocked.
- **Windows** are chosen per node from player-session telemetry, falling back to region-local 02:00 when data is thin. Fallbacks today are 18:00 UTC for the Singapore nodes, 00:00 UTC for FSN and 06:00 UTC for BHS. I did not read the production DB, so the real windows are not computed yet.
- **Freshness checks** treat a disabled timer as critical immediately, the 2026-09-15 case. An unreadable remote and unencrypted uploads are critical too. Alerts are designed to reuse `lib/fleet-alert-plan.ts` but are not wired yet.
- **Retention** is 7 daily, 4 weekly and 6 monthly for database, hypervisor and platform, and thinner for VMs by class. It never deletes for a node it could not read, and deleted-VM backups are purged 30 days after the newest copy.
- **Catch-up** for the 19-day gap is capped at 160 GiB and 60 files per run, with database and platform first. It re-plans from the remote listing each run, so it is safe to repeat.
- **Projected Dropbox usage** is about 0.9 TB, around 30% of 3 TiB. That is an upper bound built on assumptions stated in the design doc.

## What is built (inert)

- **Scripts** in `scripts/backup/`: the gate, the planner, the window-aware node runner (flag `NXEON_BACKUP_V2`, inert by default), hypervisor and platform snapshot scripts, and the `age` crypt helper.
- **Libraries** in `lib/`: `backup-layout.ts`, `backup-offsite-plan.ts`, `backup-window.ts`, `backup-freshness.ts` and `backup-stream.ts`.
- **Node-agent:** a read-only `GET /v1/backup/health`.
- **Tests:** 9 backup test files. They found four real bugs, all fixed:
  - `vzdump` runs as `perl /usr/bin/vzdump`, so the gate missed it.
  - `date -d "@N -1 day"` is invalid, which would have broken windows that cross midnight.
  - `rclone rcat` uploads an empty object when `age` dies.
  - The EPIPE error hid the real cause.

## What remains

1. Test for the agent health endpoint, then `tsc --noEmit`.
2. Agent client call and a local collector for the primary.
3. Uploader CLI `scripts/backup-offsite-run.ts`, plan-only by default.
4. Worker freshness sweep (`worker/offsite-backup-sweep.ts`, flag `NXEON_OFFSITE_FRESHNESS`), and the admin panel in `/admin/backups`.
5. Read-only window-report and policy-export scripts for the owner to run.
6. `deploy/backup/` units and timers, including the missing off-site timer file, a resource-limit slice and a `vzdump.conf` template.
7. Weekly restore-test script, using a never-reused scratch VMID.
8. Rewrite `docs/DISASTER-RECOVERY.md`, add the `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` section, and tick `ROADMAP.md`.
9. Finish the design doc: the Proxmox Backup Server evaluation, the ZFS send/recv option, data-only game backups, rollout stages and rollback.

I could not verify real quiet windows from production telemetry, the Dropbox plan after the trial, a real Dropbox upload, or a restore from an encrypted archive on a real node.

## Decisions for you

- **Key custody:** where the age private key lives. I suggest a password manager, a printed paper copy, and a second escrow recipient held elsewhere. It must never be on any server.
- **Second copy:** whether to add a write-only or immutable copy of the critical set at another provider.
- **Dropbox:** whether it stays the vault, and the plan after the trial ends (around 2026-10-12).
- **Node-5, before anything is enabled there:** create a ZFS dataset `data/backup` mounted at `/tank/backup`.
- **Off-site RPO:** 7 days for customer VPS and game VMs in this design, versus the earlier "daily". Daily game data needs the data-only engine, which is not built.
- **Customer on-demand backups:** whether they should go off-site.
- **Mirror:** whether to retire `/tank/backup/nodes` once streaming upload is proven.
- **Purge window:** how long deleted customers' backups stay (default 30 days).
- **Cleanup:** approval to delete about 60 GB of orphan local archives.
- **Manual folder:** someone created `manual-catchup-2026-10-03/` on Dropbox, so check whether it should stay.

content.thinking:
Now I'm looking at the backup unit configs — setting resource limits on the backup slice (CPU/IO weight, memory caps, task limits) and configuring the backup run service with low priority scheduling and idle IO class for zstd compression during vzdump jobs.

I'm thinking through the timer schedule (every 15 minutes, no persistence, minimal randomized delay), making sure the memory cap applies only to the vzdump process itself rather than the QEMU backup running in the VM's own cgroup. For offsite backups, I'm deciding to keep retention application opt-in via an environment variable and drop-in config, pulling node list data from the app's database env file.

I'm also scheduling the offsite upload timer to start roughly 30 minutes after the primary backup window typically ends, relying on the uploader's own gating logic rather than precise timing. Finally I'm designing a freshness watchdog service that checks whether the offsite timer is active, whether the last successful upload is under 48 hours old, and whether the inventory file is recent enough, failing loudly to trigger an alert if any check fails, running every 6 hours.

For the platform snapshot unit, I'm working out how to gate execution using ExecCondition so the gate script's exit codes (10/11) cause the unit to skip quietly rather than fail, which gives cleaner semantics than treating a skip as a failure.

I also need to add weekly restore-test timers and handle the vzdump.conf defaults — bwlimit, ionice, zstd settings — but realize these apply globally to all vzdump jobs, including customer-initiated backups through the portal, which means my throttling settings would slow customer backups too. That's worth flagging as a tradeoff since bwlimit only affects backup speed, not restore.

I'm reconsidering the plan: keep vzdump.conf conservative with just max-workers, zstd, lockwait, stopwait, and mail notification settings, and deliberately omit bwlimit from the config so it only applies via the runner's cmdline instead of impacting customer-initiated backups.

I also need to think through example config files for the backup environment, window, recipients, and policy, plus documentation — putting install steps into the design and DR docs rather than creating a standalone README, since "never proactively create docs" but install steps are part of the task. For the install script itself, I want to default to dry-run mode with an explicit --apply flag so nothing gets changed on a node without confirmation.

The install script should only list the actions it would perform and print the enable commands for timers rather than actually enabling them, keeping things conservative. Now I want to move on to writing the freshness-watch script along with its test and systemd units.
