cd /tank/nxeon-wt-backups; mkdir -p deploy/backup; cd deploy/backup
cat > nxeon-backup.slice <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon backup jobs (resource-capped so customers never feel them)
# Everything backup-related on a node runs in this slice. NOTE: on these NVMe drives the block scheduler is `none`,
# so IOWeight= has NO effect (it needs BFQ/iocost). The effective limits are CPU, memory and - the one that matters
# for reads - vzdump --bwlimit set by nxeon-backup-node.sh. A device cap can be added per node with the example drop-in
# nxeon-backup-run.service.d/io-limit.conf.example.

[Slice]
CPUWeight=10
IOWeight=10
MemoryHigh=1536M
MemoryMax=2G
TasksMax=512
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-run.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon node backup runner (window-aware, gated, one job at a time)
Wants=pve-cluster.service
After=pve-cluster.service pvedaemon.service
OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Slice=nxeon-backup.slice
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/nxeon/backup.env
ExecStart=/opt/nxeon/scripts/backup/nxeon-backup-node.sh
Nice=19
IOSchedulingClass=idle
CPUQuota=150%
# window (<=12 h) + 30 min grace. The script enforces its own hard stop at the window end; this only
# guards a wedged process, and a Type=oneshot without it would sit "activating" forever and block every tick.
TimeoutStartSec=12h30m
# Exit 0 = ok, nothing to do, or deferred by the gate. Exit 1 = a vzdump failed (alert).
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-run.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon node backup runner tick (does nothing outside this node's window)

[Timer]
# Cheap tick: the script exits in milliseconds unless we are inside the node's window and work is left.
# A window change (/etc/nxeon/backup-window.json) needs no timer change. Persistent=false on purpose: catching
# up missed ticks would just start the runner at a random hour, which the window check would refuse anyway.
OnCalendar=*:0/15
AccuracySec=1min
Persistent=false

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF
mkdir -p nxeon-backup-run.service.d
cat > nxeon-backup-run.service.d/io-limit.conf.example <<'EOF'
# OPTIONAL per-node drop-in (copy to /etc/systemd/system/nxeon-backup-run.service.d/io-limit.conf, edit the device).
# Caps the runner's own WRITES (the compressed archive) with the cgroup io controller, which works with scheduler=none.
# Find the device that backs /tank/backup:  lsblk -no PKNAME $(findmnt -no SOURCE /tank/backup)  (ZFS: the pool's disks).
# Reads of guest disks happen inside QEMU and are limited by vzdump --bwlimit, not by this.
[Service]
IOWriteBandwidthMax=/dev/sda 60M
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-offsite.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon off-site backup upload (encrypted, throttled, sequential) - PRIMARY only
After=network-online.target postgresql.service
Wants=network-online.target
OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Slice=nxeon-backup.slice
WorkingDirectory=/opt/nxeon
EnvironmentFile=/opt/nxeon/.env
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env
Environment=NXEON_OFFSITE_V2=1
Nice=19
IOSchedulingClass=idle
CPUQuota=100%
# One file at a time through age + rclone; bwlimit (NXEON_OFFSITE_BWLIMIT, default 15M) bounds the run. The
# uploader itself stops on a busy/aborting gate; this bounds a wedged connection.
TimeoutStartSec=10h
# Retention deletes nothing unless you add --apply-retention in a drop-in (see DISASTER-RECOVERY.md, rollout step 8).
ExecStart=/usr/bin/npx tsx scripts/backup-offsite-run.ts --execute --retention
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-offsite.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Daily Nxeon off-site backup upload

# This file did NOT exist in the repo: the live timer lived only in /etc/systemd/system and was stopped+disabled on
# 2026-09-15, after which nothing replicated for 19 days and nothing noticed. It is now versioned here, and
# nxeon-backup-freshness.timer + the worker's OFFSITE-BACKUP:TIMER alert fire if it is ever disabled again.
[Timer]
# Start after the PRIMARY's backup window has closed (default windows end by 22:00 UTC in SGP, later nodes follow).
# The uploader asks the gate before every file, so an overlap just pauses it.
OnCalendar=*-*-* 00:30:00
RandomizedDelaySec=15min
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-platform.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon platform snapshot (secrets, nginx, certs, git bundle, pg globals, DNS export) - PRIMARY only
OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Slice=nxeon-backup.slice
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/nxeon/backup.env
# Skip (quietly, not a failure) when the gate says the node is busy; the freshness check alerts if it stays skipped.
# systemd: ExecCondition exit 1..254 = "condition false, skip", >=255 = failure.
ExecCondition=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/nxeon/scripts/backup/nxeon-backup-gate.py --sample-seconds 3
ExecStart=/opt/nxeon/scripts/backup/nxeon-platform-snapshot.sh
Nice=19
IOSchedulingClass=idle
CPUQuota=100%
TimeoutStartSec=1h
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-platform.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nightly Nxeon platform snapshot

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 00:00:00
RandomizedDelaySec=10min
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-freshness.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon backup watchdog (independent of the worker): fails loudly if backups stopped
OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/nxeon/backup.env
ExecStart=/opt/nxeon/scripts/backup/nxeon-backup-freshness-watch.sh
Nice=10
TimeoutStartSec=5min
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-freshness.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon backup watchdog (every 6 hours)

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 00,06,12,18:20:00
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-restore-test.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon weekly restore test (one DB dump + one VM archive into scratch targets, then destroyed)
OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Slice=nxeon-backup.slice
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/nxeon/backup.env
ExecCondition=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/nxeon/scripts/backup/nxeon-backup-gate.py --sample-seconds 3
ExecStart=/opt/nxeon/scripts/backup/nxeon-restore-test.sh
Nice=19
IOSchedulingClass=idle
TimeoutStartSec=3h
EOF
cat > nxeon-backup-restore-test.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon weekly restore test

[Timer]
# Run on a node with headroom (NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_ENABLED=1 only there - see backup.env.example). Sunday small hours UTC.
OnCalendar=Sun *-*-* 03:00:00
RandomizedDelaySec=30min
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF
cat > vzdump.conf.template <<'EOF'
# /etc/vzdump.conf template for Nxeon nodes (install by hand; review first).
# These apply to EVERY vzdump on the node, including customers' on-demand backups from the portal, so they only
# bound resource use and never slow a customer's own restore. The throttle for the platform's nightly runs
# (--bwlimit 60 MiB/s, 20 on starved nodes) is passed on the command line by nxeon-backup-node.sh, deliberately NOT here.
# Compression threads: 1 (default is half the cores = a visible CPU spike on the hypervisor).
zstd: 1
# One disk read stream per guest instead of several.
performance: max-workers=1
# Never wait long on a busy lock; the runner retries next tick.
lockwait: 5
stopwait: 5
# ionice only has an effect with BFQ; harmless on NVMe (scheduler none). Kept for HDD pools.
ionice: 7
mailnotification: failure
EOF
cat > backup.env.example <<'EOF'
# /etc/nxeon/backup.env  (mode 0600) - read by the backup units on every node. EVERYTHING is off until you set it.
# Flip this ONLY after the rollout checklist (design doc section 9) for this node: it swaps the legacy
# nxeon-backup-vms.timer for the window-aware runner. Until then the runner logs "inert" and does nothing.
NXEON_BACKUP_V2=0
# Window: set by `npx tsx scripts/backup-window-report.ts` (read-only) -> /etc/nxeon/backup-window.json; these are the fallback.
NXEON_BACKUP_WINDOW_START_UTC=02:00
NXEON_BACKUP_WINDOW_HOURS=4
# Throttle for nightly vzdump (KiB/s): normal and "gentle" (node is memory-starved: primary, node-4).
NXEON_BACKUP_BWLIMIT_NORMAL_KBPS=61440
NXEON_BACKUP_BWLIMIT_GENTLE_KBPS=20480
# Gate: how long to wait for a busy node before stopping for the night.
NXEON_BACKUP_PAUSE_MAX_MIN=30
# Local retention for the hypervisor snapshot.
NXEON_HYPERVISOR_BACKUP_KEEP=7
# --- primary only ---
# NXEON_OFFSITE_BWLIMIT="08:00,10M 23:00,30M"   # rclone timetable (server local time); default 15M flat
# NXEON_OFFSITE_BYTE_BUDGET=171798691840        # bytes per run (160 GiB); catch-up spreads over nights
# OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE=dropbox:nxeon-backups
# NXEON_OFFSITE_FRESHNESS=1                     # in /opt/nxeon/.env for the WORKER: enables the freshness sweep + alerts
# --- the node chosen for the weekly restore test only (needs RAM + disk headroom) ---
# NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_ENABLED=1
# NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_STORAGE=vmdata
EOF
echo '{"startUtc":"18:00","hours":4}' > backup-window.json.example
cat > backup-recipients.txt.example <<'EOF'
# /etc/nxeon/backup-recipients.txt on the PRIMARY: age PUBLIC keys, one per line. Never a secret key
# (nxeon-backup-crypt.sh and the uploader refuse the file if it contains AGE-SECRET-KEY).
# Generate on the OWNER'S OWN machine:  scripts/backup/nxeon-backup-crypt.sh keygen identity.txt recipients.txt
# Keep identity.txt OFF every server (password manager + printed copy). Add a SECOND escrow recipient held elsewhere.
age1replacewithyourpublickeyxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
EOF

    "105": { "class": "infra" },

  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Independent backup watchdog (runs from nxeon-backup-freshness.timer on the PRIMARY, every 6 h).
# It does NOT depend on the worker or the web app: if those are down it still fails the unit, and the unit's
# OnFailure=nxeon-alert@ raises the admin notification. It checks STATE AND AGE, never "did the last run exit 0" -
# the 2026-09-15 incident was a timer that never ran, which can never fail.
#
#   1. nxeon-backup-offsite.timer must be enabled AND active
#   2. offsite.json: last successful upload must be younger than NXEON_WATCH_OFFSITE_MAX_H (default 50 h), ok must not be false,
#      and encrypted must not be false
#   3. at least one local backup timer (nxeon-backup-run.timer or the legacy nxeon-backup-vms.timer) must be enabled and active
#   4. the backup filesystem must have >= 10% free
# Exit 0 = healthy, 1 = at least one FAIL line (printed).
set -uo pipefail
STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
ROOT="${NXEON_BACKUP_ROOT:-/tank/backup}"
MAX_H="${NXEON_WATCH_OFFSITE_MAX_H:-50}"
NOW="${NXEON_WATCH_NOW:-$(date -u +%s)}"
fail=0
bad() { echo "FAIL: $*"; fail=1; }

tstate() {  # unit -> "enabled/active"
    local e a
    e="$(systemctl is-enabled "$1" 2>/dev/null)"; a="$(systemctl is-active "$1" 2>/dev/null)"
    echo "${e:-unknown}/${a:-unknown}"
}

st="$(tstate nxeon-backup-offsite.timer)"
[ "${st}" = "enabled/active" ] || bad "nxeon-backup-offsite.timer is ${st} - nothing is being copied off this chassis (systemctl enable --now nxeon-backup-offsite.timer)"

if [ -f "${STATUS_DIR}/offsite.json" ]; then
    out="$(python3 - "${STATUS_DIR}/offsite.json" "${NOW}" "${MAX_H}" <<'PY'
import json, sys, datetime
p, now, max_h = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), float(sys.argv[3])
d = json.load(open(p))
msgs = []
ls = d.get("lastSuccessAt")
if not ls:
    msgs.append("offsite.json has no lastSuccessAt: no successful upload has ever been recorded")
else:
    t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(ls.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
    h = (now - t) / 3600.0
    if h > max_h:
        msgs.append("last successful off-site upload was %.0f h ago (limit %.0f h)" % (h, max_h))
if d.get("ok") is False:
    msgs.append("last upload run FAILED: %s" % d.get("detail", "see journalctl -u nxeon-backup-offsite"))
if d.get("encrypted") is False:
    msgs.append("uploads are NOT encrypted")
print("\n".join(msgs))
PY
)"
    [ -z "${out}" ] || while IFS= read -r l; do bad "${l}"; done <<< "${out}"
else
    bad "${STATUS_DIR}/offsite.json is missing - the uploader has never reported"
fi

run="$(tstate nxeon-backup-run.timer)"; legacy="$(tstate nxeon-backup-vms.timer)"
if [ "${run}" != "enabled/active" ] && [ "${legacy}" != "enabled/active" ]; then
    bad "no local backup timer is running (nxeon-backup-run.timer ${run}, nxeon-backup-vms.timer ${legacy})"
fi

if [ -d "${ROOT}" ]; then
    pct="$(df -P "${ROOT}" | awk 'NR==2{gsub("%","",$5); print 100-$5}')"
    [ -n "${pct}" ] && [ "${pct}" -lt 10 ] && bad "${ROOT} has only ${pct}% free"
fi

[ "${fail}" = "0" ] && echo "ok: backups healthy"
exit "${fail}"
EOF
cat > nxeon-restore-test.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Weekly restore test. Proves that what we back up can actually be restored, without touching anything real:
#
#   1. DB   newest local dump -> scratch database (created, checked, dropped)
#   2. VM   one small archive from /tank/backup/platform (rotating weekly) -> scratch VMID with `qmrestore --unique 1`
#           (new MACs), NEVER started, config + disk verified, then destroyed
#   3. OFF-SITE (NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_OFFSITE=1) download the newest primary manifest + one small object and compare
#           its sha256 with the manifest (proves the off-site copy is intact). It cannot DECRYPT: the private key is
#           deliberately not on any server. The owner's monthly decrypt drill is in docs/DISASTER-RECOVERY.md.
#
# Scratch VMIDs come from a persisted counter starting at 9900000 (a range the provisioner never allocates; the
# counter is advanced BEFORE use and never goes back, so an id is never reused). Only a VMID this run allocated
# and verified absent is ever destroyed.
#
#   nxeon-restore-test.sh --dry-run    print what would be done; change nothing, write no status
# Enabled only where NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_ENABLED=1 (a node with RAM + disk headroom). Result: $STATUS_DIR/restore-test.json
set -uo pipefail
DRY=0; [ "${1:-}" = "--dry-run" ] && DRY=1
ENABLED="${NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_ENABLED:-0}"
STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
DB_DIR="${NXEON_DB_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/db}"
ARCH_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
STATE_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATE_DIR:-/var/lib/nxeon-backup}"
STORAGE="${NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_STORAGE:-vmdata}"
MAX_VM_BYTES="${NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_MAX_BYTES:-4294967296}"
COUNTER="${STATE_DIR}/restore-test-vmid"
VMID_BASE=9900000
QM="${NXEON_QM_BIN:-qm}"; QMRESTORE="${NXEON_QMRESTORE_BIN:-qmrestore}"
PSQL_AS="${NXEON_PSQL_AS:-sudo -u postgres}"
log() { echo "[$(date -u +%FT%TZ)] $*"; }

if [ "${ENABLED}" != "1" ]; then log "restore test not enabled on this node (NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_ENABLED!=1) - nothing done"; exit 0; fi

res_db="skipped"; res_vm="skipped"; res_off="skipped"; err=""; vmid=""; scratch_db=""
cleanup() {
    [ "${DRY}" = "1" ] && return
    if [ -n "${scratch_db}" ]; then ${PSQL_AS} psql -qAtc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS \"${scratch_db}\"" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
    if [ -n "${vmid}" ] && [ "${vmid}" -ge "${VMID_BASE}" ]; then ${QM} destroy "${vmid}" --purge 1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

write_status() {
    [ "${DRY}" = "1" ] && return
    local ok="$1"; mkdir -p "${STATUS_DIR}"
    local last="null"
    if [ "${ok}" = "true" ]; then last="\"$(date -u +%FT%TZ)\""
    elif [ -f "${STATUS_DIR}/restore-test.json" ]; then last="$(python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get('lastSuccessAt')))" "${STATUS_DIR}/restore-test.json" 2>/dev/null || echo null)"; fi
    printf '{"ok":%s,"at":"%s","lastSuccessAt":%s,"db":"%s","vm":"%s","offsite":"%s","vmid":"%s","error":"%s"}\n' "${ok}" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "${last}" "${res_db}" "${res_vm}" "${res_off}" "${vmid}" "${err}" > "${STATUS_DIR}/restore-test.json.tmp" \
        && mv "${STATUS_DIR}/restore-test.json.tmp" "${STATUS_DIR}/restore-test.json" && chmod 644 "${STATUS_DIR}/restore-test.json"
}
fail() { err="$*"; log "FAIL: $*"; write_status false; exit 1; }

# ---- 1. database -----------------------------------------------------------------
dump="$(ls -1t "${DB_DIR}"/nxeon-[0-9]*.sql.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
[ -n "${dump}" ] || fail "no database dump in ${DB_DIR}"
scratch_db="nxeon_restore_test_$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
log "DB: ${dump} -> scratch database ${scratch_db}"
if [ "${DRY}" = "1" ]; then log "DRY RUN - would gunzip -t, createdb, restore, count tables, drop"; res_db="dry-run"
else
    gunzip -t "${dump}" || fail "dump ${dump} is not a valid gzip"
    ${PSQL_AS} createdb "${scratch_db}" || fail "could not create scratch database"
    gunzip -c "${dump}" | ${PSQL_AS} psql -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=0 -d "${scratch_db}" >/dev/null 2>"${STATE_DIR}/restore-test.psql.err"
    tables="$(${PSQL_AS} psql -qAt -d "${scratch_db}" -c "select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [ "${tables:-0}" -ge 20 ] || fail "restored database has only ${tables:-0} tables (expected >= 20)"
    res_db="ok(${tables} tables)"
fi

# ---- 2. one VM archive --------------------------------------------------------------
week="$(date -u +%V)"
mapfile -t cands < <(find "${ARCH_DIR}" -maxdepth 1 -name 'vzdump-qemu-[0-9]*.vma.zst' -size -"$((MAX_VM_BYTES / 1024))"k -printf '%s %p\n' 2>/dev/null | grep -v 'vzdump-qemu-9[0-9][0-9][0-9]-' | sort -k2 | awk '{print $2}')
if [ "${#cands[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then fail "no VM archive under $((MAX_VM_BYTES / 1048576)) MiB to test"; fi
archive="${cands[$(( 10#${week} % ${#cands[@]} ))]}"
if [ "${DRY}" = "1" ]; then
    log "VM: would restore ${archive} to scratch VMID ${VMID_BASE}+ (counter ${COUNTER}) with: ${QMRESTORE} <archive> <vmid> --storage ${STORAGE} --unique 1 ; verify config+disk ; qm destroy --purge"
    res_vm="dry-run"
else
    mkdir -p "${STATE_DIR}"
    cur="$(cat "${COUNTER}" 2>/dev/null || echo $((VMID_BASE - 1)))"
    case "${cur}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail "corrupt VMID counter ${COUNTER}";; esac
    [ "${cur}" -ge $((VMID_BASE - 1)) ] || cur=$((VMID_BASE - 1))
    next=$((cur + 1))
    echo "${next}" > "${COUNTER}.tmp" && mv "${COUNTER}.tmp" "${COUNTER}"     # advance BEFORE use: never reused even if we crash
    if ${QM} status "${next}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then fail "scratch VMID ${next} already exists - refusing (counter stays advanced)"; fi
    vmid="${next}"
    log "VM: restoring ${archive} -> scratch VMID ${vmid} on ${STORAGE} (never started)"
    ${QMRESTORE} "${archive}" "${vmid}" --storage "${STORAGE}" --unique 1 >/dev/null 2>"${STATE_DIR}/restore-test.qm.err" || fail "qmrestore failed: $(head -c 200 "${STATE_DIR}/restore-test.qm.err")"
    ${QM} config "${vmid}" 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^(scsi|virtio|sata|ide)[0-9]+:' || fail "restored VM ${vmid} has no disk in its config"
    res_vm="ok(vmid ${vmid}, $(basename "${archive}"))"
fi

# ---- 3. off-site integrity (optional) -----------------------------------------------
if [ "${NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_OFFSITE:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    remote="${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE:-dropbox:nxeon-backups}"
    if [ "${DRY}" = "1" ]; then log "OFFSITE: would fetch the newest primary manifest from ${remote} and sha256-compare one database object"; res_off="dry-run"
    else
        newest="$(rclone lsf -R --files-only "${remote}" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[0-9]{4}/[0-9-]{10}/primary/manifest\.json$' | sort | tail -1)"
        [ -n "${newest}" ] || fail "no primary manifest found off-site"
        rclone cat "${remote}/${newest}" > "${STATE_DIR}/offsite-manifest.json" 2>/dev/null || fail "could not read ${newest}"
        read -r rel want < <(python3 -c "
import json,sys
m=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
it=sorted([i for i in m['items'] if i['category']=='database'], key=lambda i:i['bytes'])
print(it[0]['path'], it[0]['sha256']) if it else print('', '')" "${STATE_DIR}/offsite-manifest.json")
        [ -n "${rel}" ] || fail "newest primary manifest lists no database object"
        got="$(rclone cat "${remote}/$(dirname "${newest}")/${rel}" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)"
        [ "${got}" = "${want}" ] || fail "off-site object ${rel} sha256 ${got} != manifest ${want}"
        res_off="ok(${rel})"
    fi
fi

[ "${DRY}" = "1" ] && { log "dry run complete"; exit 0; }
write_status true
log "restore test passed: db=${res_db} vm=${res_vm} offsite=${res_off}"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x nxeon-backup-freshness-watch.sh nxeon-restore-test.sh; bash -n nxeon-backup-freshness-watch.sh && bash -n nxeon-restore-test.sh && echo ok

    gunzip -t "${dump}" || fail "dump ${dump} is not a valid gzip"
    ${PSQL_AS} createdb "${scratch_db}" || fail "could not create scratch database"
    gunzip -c "${dump}" | ${PSQL_AS} psql -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=0 -d "${scratch_db}" >/dev/null 2>"${STATE_DIR}/restore-test.psql.err"
    tables="$(${PSQL_AS} psql -qAt -d "${scratch_db}" -c "select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [ "${tables:-0}" -ge 20 ] || fail "restored database has only ${tables:-0} tables (expected >= 20)"
    res_db="ok(${tables} tables)"
fi

# ---- 2. one VM archive --------------------------------------------------------------
week="$(date -u +%V)"
mapfile -t cands < <(find "${ARCH_DIR}" -maxdepth 1 -name 'vzdump-qemu-[0-9]*.vma.zst' -size -"$((MAX_VM_BYTES / 1024))"k -printf '%s %p\n' 2>/dev/null | grep -v 'vzdump-qemu-9[0-9][0-9][0-9]-' | sort -k2 | awk '{print $2}')
if [ "${#cands[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then fail "no VM archive under $((MAX_VM_BYTES / 1048576)) MiB to test"; fi
archive="${cands[$(( 10#${week} % ${#cands[@]} ))]}"
if [ "${DRY}" = "1" ]; then
    log "VM: would restore ${archive} to scratch VMID ${VMID_BASE}+ (counter ${COUNTER}) with: ${QMRESTORE} <archive> <vmid> --storage ${STORAGE} --unique 1 ; verify config+disk ; qm destroy --purge"
    res_vm="dry-run"
else
    mkdir -p "${STATE_DIR}"
    cur="$(cat "${COUNTER}" 2>/dev/null || echo $((VMID_BASE - 1)))"
    case "${cur}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail "corrupt VMID counter ${COUNTER}";; esac
    [ "${cur}" -ge $((VMID_BASE - 1)) ] || cur=$((VMID_BASE - 1))
    next=$((cur + 1))
    echo "${next}" > "${COUNTER}.tmp" && mv "${COUNTER}.tmp" "${COUNTER}"     # advance BEFORE use: never reused even if we crash
    if ${QM} status "${next}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then fail "scratch VMID ${next} already exists - refusing (counter stays advanced)"; fi
    vmid="${next}"
    log "VM: restoring ${archive} -> scratch VMID ${vmid} on ${STORAGE} (never started)"
    ${QMRESTORE} "${archive}" "${vmid}" --storage "${STORAGE}" --unique 1 >/dev/null 2>"${STATE_DIR}/restore-test.qm.err" || fail "qmrestore failed: $(head -c 200 "${STATE_DIR}/restore-test.qm.err")"
    ${QM} config "${vmid}" 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^(scsi|virtio|sata|ide)[0-9]+:' || fail "restored VM ${vmid} has no disk in its config"
    res_vm="ok(vmid ${vmid}, $(basename "${archive}"))"
fi

# ---- 3. off-site integrity (optional) -----------------------------------------------
if [ "${NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_OFFSITE:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    remote="${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE:-dropbox:nxeon-backups}"
    if [ "${DRY}" = "1" ]; then log "OFFSITE: would fetch the newest primary manifest from ${remote} and sha256-compare one database object"; res_off="dry-run"
    else
        newest="$(rclone lsf -R --files-only "${remote}" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[0-9]{4}/[0-9-]{10}/primary/manifest\.json$' | sort | tail -1)"
        [ -n "${newest}" ] || fail "no primary manifest found off-site"
        rclone cat "${remote}/${newest}" > "${STATE_DIR}/offsite-manifest.json" 2>/dev/null || fail "could not read ${newest}"
        read -r rel want < <(python3 -c "
import json,sys
m=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
it=sorted([i for i in m['items'] if i['category']=='database'], key=lambda i:i['bytes'])
print(it[0]['path'], it[0]['sha256']) if it else print('', '')" "${STATE_DIR}/offsite-manifest.json")
        [ -n "${rel}" ] || fail "newest primary manifest lists no database object"
        got="$(rclone cat "${remote}/$(dirname "${newest}")/${rel}" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)"
        [ "${got}" = "${want}" ] || fail "off-site object ${rel} sha256 ${got} != manifest ${want}"
        res_off="ok(${rel})"
    fi
fi

[ "${DRY}" = "1" ] && { log "dry run complete"; exit 0; }
write_status true
log "restore test passed: db=${res_db} vm=${res_vm} offsite=${res_off}"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x nxeon-backup-freshness-watch.sh nxeon-restore-test.sh; bash -n nxeon-backup-freshness-watch.sh && bash -n nxeon-restore-test.sh && echo ok

f0a4a1a413 Read-only window report and policy export scripts; tsc clean
# Disaster recovery — restoring Nxeon from the off-site (Dropbox) backups

Read this if a chassis is gone, wiped, or compromised, and you need to bring the platform back from
nothing but the Dropbox copy. It is a manual, deliberate procedure — there is no single "restore
everything" command, on purpose: a real disaster-recovery restore should never run unattended, since
the operator needs to make real judgment calls at several points below (which node a VM belongs on,
whether a compromised box's credentials need rotating before they're trusted again, etc.).

See `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`'s "Multi-node disaster-recovery backups" section for how these backups are
*produced*. This document is only about getting them back.

## What's already proven to work, today, unattended

`scripts/verify-restore.sh` (`nxeon-verify-restore.timer`, daily) already restores the newest **local**
database dump into a real scratch database and asserts core tables came back with real rows — every
day, automatically, non-destructively. If that unit is green, the database dump format itself is proven
restorable; you are not trusting an assumption. It does not (yet) pull the dump down from Dropbox
first — it verifies the local copy the same script that made it also relies on — so it proves the dump
is *good*, not that the *off-site copy* of it is retrievable. Steps 1-2 below are how you'd prove the
latter, and are worth rehearsing once when things are calm rather than for the first time during a real
incident.

## Where to find things on Dropbox

Backups live under `nxeon-backups/`, one folder per day the off-site job ran, named `<run-number>-
<date>` (e.g. `00001-2026-09-12`), newest run = highest number. Inside each run folder, one subfolder
per physical node:

```
nxeon-backups/
  00001-2026-09-12/
    primary/
      db/            nxeon-<date>.sql.gz, nxeon_staging-<date>.sql.gz
      host-config/   host-config-<date>.tar.gz  (/etc/pve, /etc/nxeon, /opt/nxeon/.env, network config)
      vms/           vzdump-qemu-<vmid>-<date>.vma.zst + .log, for every VM/template on primary
    node-2/
      platform/      host-config-<date>.tar.gz, vzdump-qemu-<vmid>-<date>.vma.zst + .log
      status/        vm-backup.json, host-config.json (machine-readable, not needed for a restore)
    node-3/
      platform/ ...
      status/ ...
  00002-2026-09-13/
    ...
```

Each run only contains files that were *new* that day — a VM's most recent backup might be in an
earlier run-folder than the newest one if nothing changed since. **To find the newest copy of anything,
check run-folders from the highest number downward until you find it** — don't assume everything you
need is in the latest folder. A one-time legacy `db/`, `host-config/`, `vms/` flat folder set (no run
number) may also exist from before this dated-folder scheme was introduced (2026-09-12) — check there
too if you're restoring from before that date.

Pull anything down with `rclone`, configured on whichever machine you're restoring from (root's
`~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf`, same OAuth setup as production — see docs/DOCUMENTATION.md):

```bash
rclone lsf -R dropbox:nxeon-backups/                     # see everything that exists
rclone copy dropbox:nxeon-backups/00001-2026-09-12/primary/db/ ./restore/db/
```

## 1. Restoring the database

```bash
rclone copy "dropbox:nxeon-backups/<run>/primary/db/nxeon-<date>.sql.gz" ./
gunzip nxeon-<date>.sql.gz
# On the new/target Postgres instance:
sudo -u postgres createdb nxeon
sudo -u postgres psql nxeon < nxeon-<date>.sql
```

This is exactly what `verify-restore.sh` does against a scratch database every night (with `nxeon`
swapped for a throwaway name) — the same command is already proven to work daily, just against the
local copy rather than one pulled from Dropbox.

Then point `/opt/nxeon/.env`'s `DATABASE_URL` at the restored database.

## 2. Restoring host configuration (`/etc/pve`, `/etc/nxeon`, `/opt/nxeon/.env`)

```bash
rclone copy "dropbox:nxeon-backups/<run>/primary/host-config/host-config-<date>.tar.gz" ./
tar -tzf host-config-<date>.tar.gz | less        # inspect before extracting anything onto a live host
```

This archive contains `/etc/pve/priv` (cluster and CA private keys) and `/etc/nxeon` (Proxmox API
token, Cloudflare token, mail credentials) — **treat it as a bundle of live secrets**, not just config
files. On a genuinely fresh Proxmox host:

- `/etc/pve/qemu-server/<vmid>.conf` (under `etc/pve/nodes/<node>/qemu-server/` inside the archive —
  see `scripts/backup-pve-config.sh`'s own note on why: `/etc/pve/qemu-server` is a symlink into
  `nodes/<node>/qemu-server`, and tar stores the symlink target's real path, not the symlink itself)
  tells you each VM's RAM, disks, NIC/bridge, boot order — needed before `qmrestore` (step 3) can
  recreate a VM identically.
- `/etc/pve/storage.cfg` tells you what each storage ID (`vmdata`, `vmdata-hdd`, `backup`, ...) should
  point at — recreate matching `pvesm add` entries on the new host BEFORE restoring VMs, or `qmrestore`
  will fail looking for a storage ID it doesn't recognize (this is the exact class of bug found and
  fixed on node-2/node-3 on 2026-09-12 — see docs/DOCUMENTATION.md — a template referencing a storage
  ID that was never created on that host).
- `etc/network/interfaces`, `etc/hostname`, `etc/hosts`, `etc/fstab` — the low-level host identity;
  compare against the new hardware rather than blindly overwriting (a restored `interfaces` file
  written for the OLD NIC names/bridges can take a fresh host off the network).
- `/opt/nxeon/.env` — restore this only onto the primary (it's the app's own secrets: DB URL,
  AUTH_SECRET, Stripe/Anthropic/Cloudflare keys). **Rotate every credential in it if the loss was due
  to a compromise, not just a hardware failure** — see the standing live-credential-rotation policy;
  a secret that was on a compromised disk should never be trusted again as-is.
- The `state/` directory inside the archive (`pveversion.txt`, `pvesm-status.txt`, `qm-list.txt`,
  `zpool-status.txt`, `zfs-list.txt`, `ip-addr.txt`, `ip-route.txt`, `iptables-save.txt`,
  `nxeon-units.txt`, `lsblk.txt`) is plain-text, human-read state captured at backup time — this is
  what a person reconstructing the host from memory actually needs, not just the raw config files.

## 3. Restoring a VM from a `vzdump` archive

```bash
rclone copy "dropbox:nxeon-backups/<run>/primary/vms/vzdump-qemu-<vmid>-<date>.vma.zst" ./
# or, for a node-2/node-3 VM:
rclone copy "dropbox:nxeon-backups/<run>/node-2/platform/vzdump-qemu-<vmid>-<date>.vma.zst" ./

qmrestore vzdump-qemu-<vmid>-<date>.vma.zst <new-vmid> --storage <target-storage-id>
```

`qmrestore` reads the guest's own disk/RAM/NIC definition out of the archive itself — it does NOT need
the host-config archive for that part. It DOES need `--storage` to already exist on the target host
(step 2's storage.cfg restoration), and — per `[[Never reuse VM IDs]]` — allocate a fresh, never-used
VMID rather than reusing the original one, exactly the same rule that already applies to normal
provisioning.

**Restoring onto a brand-new node** (the chassis itself is gone, not just its disk): run
`scripts/onboard-node.sh` first to get storages/firewall/node-agent/local-backups set up correctly
(see docs/DOCUMENTATION.md's "Adding node N" runbook), THEN restore VMs onto it — do not `qmrestore`

sec='''

## Off-site backups v2 (2026-10-04, branch `feature/complete-offsite-backups`) - complete, encrypted, gated, windowed

**Status: built, tested, INERT. Nothing is enabled until the owner follows the rollout in `/root/research/backup-design.md` section 9.** Why: on 2026-10-03 the off-site timer had been disabled for 19 days with no alert, VM archives on Dropbox were 3 weeks old, nodes 4 and 5 had never reached off-site, node-5's backup directory sat on a 20 GB root filesystem, and everything uploaded (including `/etc/pve/priv`, Cloudflare tokens and `.env`) was unencrypted.

**What is backed up (per category).** *Hypervisor* (`scripts/backup/nxeon-hypervisor-snapshot.sh`, every node): `/etc/pve`, network + nft/iptables, systemd units, ZFS layout and local properties, ARC caps, ssh host keys, node-agent files, cloud-init snippets, package lists, partition tables. *VMs*: `vzdump` per guest, snapshot mode, classed by `scripts/backup/nxeon-backup-plan.py` (infra: daily off-site; customer VPS and game: weekly; templates: monthly from the primary only). *Databases*: the existing dumps plus `pg_dumpall --globals-only` (inside the platform snapshot). *Platform* (`nxeon-platform-snapshot.sh`, primary): `.env` and other secrets, nginx, Let's Encrypt, rclone config, a `git bundle --all` of the repo + uncommitted work, admin uploads, Cloudflare DNS zone exports.

**Layout.** `nxeon-backups/<YYYY>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<node>/{hypervisor,vms/<vmid>-<name>,databases,platform}/` + `manifest.json` + `README.txt` per run (`lib/backup-layout.ts`). Contents are `.age`-encrypted to PUBLIC keys in `/etc/nxeon/backup-recipients.txt`; the private identity is held off-box by the owner. `scripts/backup/nxeon-backup-crypt.sh` (keygen/encrypt/decrypt/check) refuses a recipients file that contains a secret key.

**Upload.** Only the primary holds the Dropbox credential. `scripts/backup-offsite-run.ts` is plan-only by default (`--plan` output lists exactly what would go); `--execute` additionally needs `NXEON_OFFSITE_V2=1`, a valid recipients file and a gate "go". It streams each file from the node-agent (`/v1/backup/file`) through `age` into `rclone rcat` (no staging on disk, no mirror on the primary), strictly one file at a time, bandwidth from `NXEON_OFFSITE_BWLIMIT`, byte budget per run (default 160 GiB; the 19-day catch-up spreads over several nights). What is already off-site is read from the remote listing (no marker file); truncated objects (<150 B) never count; a failed upload deletes whatever landed under the final name. Retention (`planRetention`, dry-run unless `--apply-retention`): db/hypervisor/platform 7 daily + 4 weekly + 6 monthly; VMs by class; deleted VMs purged 30 days after the newest copy; never deletes for a node it could not read; 400-deletion cap.

**Performance safety.** `nxeon-backup-run.timer` ticks every 15 min on each node; `nxeon-backup-node.sh` does nothing outside the node's window (`/etc/nxeon/backup-window.json`, from `scripts/backup-window-report.ts`, which measures player-session and visit hours per node), takes one `flock` (one job per node), asks `nxeon-backup-gate.py` before every unit (PSI cpu/io/memory, swap ACTIVITY, MemAvailable floor, load, other heavy jobs, ZFS ARC no-grow -> "gentle" profile at 20 MiB/s instead of 60), stops at the window's hard end and resumes next tick. `vzdump` runs with `--bwlimit --zstd 1 --performance max-workers=1`. Everything runs in `nxeon-backup.slice` (CPUWeight/CPUQuota, MemoryHigh/Max, Nice 19). `ionice`/`IOWeight` do nothing on these NVMe drives (scheduler `none`); `--bwlimit` is the real read throttle. The runner is inert unless `NXEON_BACKUP_V2=1` in `/etc/nxeon/backup.env`.

**Monitoring.** (1) `nxeon-backup-freshness.timer` (shell, independent of the worker): fails the unit (-> `nxeon-alert@`) if the off-site timer is not enabled+active, the last successful upload is older than 50 h, uploads are unencrypted, no local timer runs, or the backup filesystem is under 10% free. (2) Worker sweep `worker/offsite-backup-sweep.ts` (hourly, `NXEON_OFFSITE_FRESHNESS=1`): node-agent `GET /v1/backup/health` (read-only) per node + remote listing -> `lib/backup-freshness.ts` -> debounced, auto-resolving `NodeAlert`s with dimension prefix `OFFSITE-BACKUP:` (registered in `lib/fleet-alert-plan.ts`); an unreadable remote or node never auto-resolves anything. (3) `/admin/backups` "Off-site coverage" panel: per node and VM, newest local vs newest off-site age plus all findings; a missing or >12 h-old inventory is shown as a warning.

**Restore testing.** `nxeon-backup-restore-test.timer` (weekly, only where `NXEON_RESTORE_TEST_ENABLED=1`): newest DB dump -> scratch database; one small VM archive -> scratch VMID from a persisted never-reused counter starting at 9,900,000 (`qmrestore --unique 1`, never started, destroyed); optionally sha256-checks the newest off-site object against its manifest. It cannot decrypt (key off-box), so the owner runs a monthly decrypt drill (`docs/DISASTER-RECOVERY.md` section 9). Result in `/tank/backup/status/restore-test.json`, surfaced as the `OFFSITE-BACKUP:RESTORE-TEST` alert when old or failed.

**Files.** `scripts/backup/*`, `scripts/backup-offsite-run.ts`, `scripts/backup-window-report.ts`, `scripts/backup-policy-export.ts` (read-only DB), `deploy/backup/*` (units, timers incl. the previously missing `nxeon-backup-offsite.timer`, slice, `vzdump.conf.template`, env examples), `lib/backup-{layout,offsite-plan,window,freshness,stream,node-health,upload-run,sweep-plan,policy-export}.ts`, `lib/offsite-inventory-view.ts`, `components/admin/OffsiteCoveragePanel.tsx`, node-agent `GET /v1/backup/health` (+ `hypervisor/` and status files in the file allowlist; **agents must be redeployed on every node**). Tests: `test/backup-*.test.ts`, `test/node-agent-backup-health.test.ts`, `test/offsite-inventory-view.test.ts`.

**Known limits (honest).** Game-server data-only backups (small, daily) are designed but NOT built: until then customer VPS and game VMs have a 7-day off-site RPO (24 h local). No WAL archiving/PITR. Real quiet windows were not computed (needs a read of production telemetry by the owner). A real Dropbox upload, a real restore from an encrypted object and the live behaviour of the new units on a node are unverified. Customer on-demand backups (Proxmox `backup` storage) remain local only. The primary was root-compromised on 2026-09-06 and can delete Dropbox: a second write-only/immutable copy of tier-1 data is recommended.
'''
p='docs/DOCUMENTATION.md'
s=open(p).read().rstrip('\n')
s+=sec+'\n'
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

Real bugs the tests caught: vzdump runs as `perl /usr/bin/vzdump`; `date -d "@N -1 day"` invalid (midnight-crossing windows); rclone rcat uploads an empty object when age dies; EPIPE hid the cause.

## 5. NEW FINDINGS TO FOLD IN (owner, 2026-10-04)
- node-5's backup storage needs its own dataset FIRST (root fs 811 MB free). Rollout step 2 below makes it a hard prerequisite; the freshness DISK finding says so in its text.
- The primary is overloaded (swap full, OOM-killed VM 8000 on 09-25). Every new job is therefore: gated (gate pause -> wait <=30 min, abort -> skip the night), strictly sequential (one flock per node; the gate also refuses to start while any other vzdump/rclone/qmrestore/zfs-send runs), in a CPU/memory-capped slice, at Nice 19, and bandwidth-capped. On the primary specifically: the uploader runs AFTER the primary's local window (timer 00:30 UTC, gate-checked per file), the platform snapshot is gate-skipped when busy, restore tests are NOT enabled on the primary (pick node-5 or node-2), and the old /tank/backup/nodes mirror (extra disk + NIC load on the primary) is retired by the streaming uploader.

## 6. MONITORING (built; see section 2.8)
Three independent layers so "timer disabled" cannot be silent: (1) shell watchdog nxeon-backup-freshness.timer every 6 h -> OnFailure nxeon-alert@ (works with the worker/web down); (2) worker sweep -> NodeAlert OFFSITE-BACKUP:* via fleet-alert-plan (debounced, 24 h cooldown, auto-resolve only for nodes actually read); (3) /admin/backups panel shows local vs off-site age per VM and marks a dead checker (inventory >12 h old) in red. Alert catalogue: TIMER, ENCRYPTION, REMOTE, QUOTA, STALE:{db,platform,hypervisor,vms}, LOCAL-TIMER, LOCAL-NONE, LOCAL-STALE, DISK, AGENT, RESTORE-TEST.

## 7. RESTORE TESTING (built)
Weekly nxeon-restore-test.sh on ONE node with headroom (not the primary): newest DB dump -> scratch DB; one small VM archive -> scratch VMID from a persisted counter starting 9,900,000 (above SANDBOX_VMID_MIN 990000, so freshVmidFloor ignores it; advanced before use, never reused; only an id it allocated and verified absent is destroyed; qmrestore --unique 1; VM never started); optional sha256 check of the newest off-site object vs its manifest. Decryption cannot be tested on-box (key is off-box) -> monthly owner decrypt drill (DR doc section 9). Full rebuild-from-nothing runbook per category incl. nodes: docs/DISASTER-RECOVERY.md.

input.message:
REPORT: the off-site backup build is finished and committed, with nothing applied anywhere.

I touched no node or VM, ran no backup, upload or restore, and pushed nothing. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. The final run of 165 tests passes: 9 backup test files plus the agent-health test, the inventory-view test, `ip-fleet-alerts`, `guest-backup-coverage`, `backups-admin` and `offsite-retention`.

**Where it lives**
- Branch `feature/complete-offsite-backups`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-backups`.
- Commits, all explicit-path with hooks disabled so nothing auto-pushed: `42d4e88cdd`, `38e5306fa7`, `ddeb019997`, `647cf08090`, `f0a4a1a413`, `2ecc90e711`.
- Design, audit, coverage matrix, rollout and rollback: `/root/research/backup-design.md`.
- Status notes: `/root/agent-notes/backups.md`.
- Scratch to delete: `/tank/age-test` on the primary holds a real `age` binary I extracted but did not install. The stream and crypt tests use it via `AGE_BIN` and `AGE_KEYGEN_BIN`.

**What was built**

1. **Typecheck.** Only test typing errors, now fixed.
2. **Uploader.** `scripts/backup-offsite-run.ts` plans only by default.
   - `--execute` also needs `NXEON_OFFSITE_V2=1`, a valid recipients file and a gate "go".
   - It streams each file from the node-agent through `age` into `rclone rcat`, one at a time, and writes a manifest and README per run.
   - It merges with a half-finished manifest from the same night.
   - The planner is tested; `--execute` and real uploads were never run.
3. **Alerts and admin panel.**
   - The hourly freshness sweep (`worker/offsite-backup-sweep.ts`, flag `NXEON_OFFSITE_FRESHNESS=1`) uses the `OFFSITE-BACKUP:` prefix added to `lib/fleet-alert-plan.ts`.
   - The `/admin/backups` panel shows local vs off-site age per VM and flags a dead checker.
   - Alerts never auto-resolve for a node or remote that could not be read.
   - The inventory is a status file, not the Setting table, because Setting is shipped to the admin settings page.
   - The node-agent `GET /v1/backup/health` is now tested.
4. **`deploy/backup/`.**
   - Units and timers: run, off-site (the file that was missing), platform snapshot, freshness watchdog and restore test.
   - A resource-capped slice (CPU, memory, Nice 19).
   - `vzdump.conf.template` and example env, window, recipients and policy files.
   - Gating:
     - The platform snapshot and restore test skip quietly when the node is busy.
     - Everything is strictly sequential.
5. **Restore test.** `nxeon-restore-test.sh` has a dry-run mode and 10 tests.
   - It restores the newest DB dump to a scratch database and one small VM archive to a scratch VMID from a never-reused counter starting at 9,900,000.
   - It destroys only a VMID it allocated and found absent, and never starts the VM.
6. **Design doc.** Added the Proxmox Backup Server evaluation, the ZFS-send evaluation, the staged 12-step rollout, rollback, monitoring and restore sections, and your two new findings.
7. **Docs.** `docs/DISASTER-RECOVERY.md` is rewritten as a full rebuild runbook: key custody and recovery, hypervisor, platform, databases, VMs, every node, DNS and mail, and a monthly decrypt drill. The legacy layout is kept as an appendix. `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` has a new "Off-site backups v2" section, and `ROADMAP.md` is updated.

**Also built**
- `scripts/backup-window-report.ts` and `scripts/backup-policy-export.ts` are read-only against the DB and are for you to run; I did not run them.

**Your two new findings**
- **node-5:** its own dataset is now a hard prerequisite (rollout step 2). The disk finding says so in its text.
- **Primary overloaded:** every job is gated, strictly sequential and in the capped slice. Specifically:
  - The uploader runs after the primary's local window.
  - The platform snapshot is skipped when busy.
  - The weekly restore test is not enabled on the primary.
  - The streaming uploader retires the old `/tank/backup/nodes` mirror.

**Evaluation verdicts**
- **Proxmox Backup Server:** technically better, not worth switching now. It needs a separate host, cannot target Dropbox, and adds a dependency to the disaster path. Revisit when provisioned disk exceeds about 2 TB, or if you want daily off-site RPO without building the game-data engine.
- **ZFS send:** an optional phase 3 for the biggest guests on healthy nodes only.

**Not verified**
- Real quiet windows (the production telemetry was not read).
- Dropbox plan and quota after the trial ends around 2026-10-12.
- A real upload, a restore from an encrypted object, and the new units live on a node.
- The primary's real CPU and IO cost under load.
- `test/node-agent.test.ts` (existing) uses a throwaway iptables chain on the primary. It passed and cleaned up, but note it.

**Not built**
- Game data-only backups, so customer VPS and game VMs have a 7-day off-site RPO versus 24 h local.
- WAL/PITR.
- A second immutable copy.

**Owner rollout, in order** (design doc section 9)
1. Merge and deploy through the normal pipeline, then redeploy the node-agent on every node.
2. Give node-5 (and check every node) its own backup dataset with at least twice the largest archive free.
3. `apt install age` on the primary. Generate the main and escrow keys on your own machine and put only the public keys in `/etc/nxeon/backup-recipients.txt`. Do one decrypt drill.
4. Run the window and policy reports and copy the results to the nodes.
5. Run `npx tsx scripts/backup-offsite-run.ts --retention --verbose` and read the plan.
6. Primary: install the units, set `NXEON_BACKUP_V2=1`, enable the run and platform timers, and keep the legacy VM timer for a week.
7. Enable the off-site timer, start the first run by hand at a quiet hour, and watch 3-4 catch-up nights at 160 GiB each.
8. After a healthy week, add `--apply-retention`.
9. Move the other nodes one at a time, node-4 last.
10. Set `NXEON_OFFSITE_FRESHNESS=1` and enable the freshness timer. Test it by disabling the timer and confirming the alert.
11. Enable the weekly restore test on node-5 or node-2.
12. Take the second copy, and retire the old mirror and the legacy unencrypted Dropbox folders.

Rollback per node is instant (disable the run timer, set `NXEON_BACKUP_V2=0`, keep the legacy timer). The legacy scripts are untouched, and uploaded objects are never modified.

**Owner decisions needed**
1. **Key custody:** where the age keys live: the main key and an escrow holder. Never on any server.
2. **Second copy:** a second write-only or immutable copy of the small critical set (about 10 GB). The primary was root-compromised on 2026-09-06 and can delete Dropbox.
3. **Dropbox:** the plan after about 2026-10-12, and whether it stays the vault.
4. **Off-site RPO:** accept weekly (7 days) for customer VPS and game VMs, or fund the data-only engine.
5. **Customer on-demand backups:** whether they go off-site.
6. **Mirror:** retire `/tank/backup/nodes`.
7. **Purge window:** 30 days for deleted customers' backups, by default.
8. **Cleanup:** delete about 60 GB of orphan local archives and the unencrypted legacy Dropbox folders, after verifying the encrypted copies decrypt.
9. **Restore-test node:** which node runs it.
10. **Phase 2 or PBS:** whether to build the game data-only engine and/or trial Proxmox Backup Server.

input.message:
REPORT (resumed 2026-10-04): the off-site backup branch is rebased onto current main and green; the staged rollout runbook is written. I did not merge to main, and I changed no node or VM. I ran no backups, uploads or restores, never enabled the off-site timer, and put no secrets in logs.

**1. Branch**
- `feature/complete-offsite-backups`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-backups`. Head is `0290f5700f`, after the merge commit `5f5d0afc56`.
- I merged main (`27b6cb1156`; the 20261004T115028Z release branch is already in main). The only conflict was the append-only `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, resolved by keeping both sides.
- main added 52 lines to `prisma/schema.prisma`, so I regenerated the Prisma client inside my worktree only, with a dummy `DATABASE_URL`. The live `/opt/nxeon` client was not touched.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` shows 0 errors. 151 tests pass: the backup suite, node-agent tests, `ip-fleet-alerts`, and `backups-admin`.
- I made one fix on resume: the weekly restore test now skips its database step on a node that has no Postgres (only the primary has the dumps), instead of failing. That lets it run on node-2 or node-5. It has a new test.

**2. Rollout runbook**
- It is `docs/BACKUP-ROLLOUT.md`, with exact owner commands, a CHECK and a rollback per stage. The canary is node-2, and node-4 goes last. Node-4 is still on the legacy timer if the gate keeps aborting it.
  - **Stage 0:** merge and deploy through the normal pipeline. Nothing changes in behaviour.
  - **Stage 1:** generate two age keys (main and escrow) on your own laptop. Install only the public keys on the primary, and run a decrypt drill.
  - **Stage 2a:** give node-5 its own ZFS dataset for `/tank/backup`: create `data/backup`, rsync the existing archives in, swap the mountpoint, with rollback.
  - **Stage 2b:** copy the scripts and the new node-agent to each node, restart the agent, and install the unit files without enabling them.
  - **Stage 3:** run the read-only window and policy reports, review them, and copy per-node files. Then dry-run on the canary.
  - **Stage 4:** enable the run timer on the canary beside the legacy timer for 7 days. Then move node-3, node-5 and node-4 one at a time.
  - **Stage 5:** on the primary, platform snapshot, watchdog and freshness flag. The panel must show CRITICAL "timer not running" until stage 6; that is the alert working.
  - **Stage 6:** read the plan, do one manual upload at a quiet hour, check the tree and decrypt from the laptop, and only then enable the off-site timer.
  - **Stage 7:** retention, orphan and legacy cleanup, the restore test on node-2 or node-5, and retiring the `/tank/backup/nodes` mirror.
- New facts are folded into `/root/research/backup-design.md` (section 11).
  - Palsauge moved onto the primary, so the primary is now the busiest node. Its swap is still full (10.2/10.2 GB) with about 14.8 GB RAM free. Its backup window stays gated and away from peak.
  - Guests 114, 9550, 600 and 148 are deleted, so their archives are now orphans.
  - The `VM.Config.Options` role change does not affect backups.
  - `vzdump --bwlimit` is still the only real throttle.
- A live read-only check today showed:
  - Node-5's `/tank/backup` is still on the 20 GB root at 96% with its timer disabled.
  - Node-3, node-4 and the primary have swap full.
  - The off-site timer is disabled.
  - Dropbox has nothing new since 09-14, apart from the 10-03 manual folder.

**3. Open decisions, with my recommendation for each**
1. **Key custody:** use two age identities. The main one goes in your password manager and on paper; the escrow one goes to a second trusted person or place. Never on a server. Do a monthly decrypt drill. Without an escrow copy, one lost key makes every backup unreadable.
2. **Second immutable copy:** yes, for the database, platform snapshot and hypervisor files only (about 10-25 GB). Use object storage with Object Lock and a write-only key held on the primary, so a compromised primary cannot delete it. It costs a few dollars a month, needs you to open the account, and I have not built it.
3. **Dropbox after about 2026-10-12:** keep it only if the paid 2-3 TB plan is confirmed. Check with `rclone about dropbox:` before then. If not, switch `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` to B2 or S3, since the code is generic.
4. **RPO:** accept weekly off-site for customer VPS and game VMs in the first release; local stays daily. Fund the game data-only backup engine next if you want daily off-site for worlds. Keep infra VMs, databases, platform and hypervisor files daily.
5. **Orphan cleanup:** delete the orphan local archives (about 60 GB plus the new ones). Delete the unencrypted legacy Dropbox folders by hand, and only after a verified encrypted decrypt drill, since they hold plaintext secrets.
6. **Mirror and restore-test node:** retire `/tank/backup/nodes` after stage 6. Run the restore test on node-2, or node-5 once it has its dataset, never on the primary.

**4. Untested**
- A real Dropbox upload, especially a 10-20 GB object. Only the local rclone backend and small files were tested.
- Streaming a large file from a node-agent over the real network.
- The new systemd units on a real node. I only ran `systemd-analyze verify` locally and shell tests with stubs.
- The runner against a real `vzdump`; it ran with stubs only.
- The gate's thresholds under real backup load. I only read a baseline from three nodes.
- Window selection on production telemetry.
- The freshness sweep and alert delivery against the real database and agents. The pure logic and alert plan are tested; the worker sweep itself was never run.
- The `/admin/backups` panel in a browser. It is type-checked only.
- The node-agent health endpoint on a real Proxmox node. It was tested with stub tools.
- The restore test against real `qmrestore` and Postgres.
- The platform and hypervisor snapshot scripts. I only syntax-checked and listed them, because they read secrets.
- Retention deletes on a real remote.
- The owner-session merge and promote of this branch.
- Still not built: game data-only backups, WAL/PITR, and the second immutable copy.

Notes are in `/root/agent-notes/backups.md`. `/tank/age-test` still holds a real `age` binary I extracted for the tests; delete it when done.
